items.summary: Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in extended trading after missing profit and revenue expectations on Oct 28. Its third-quarter free cash flow was negative US$9.07 billion, up from US$5.9 billion a quarter earlier. Total revenue reached US$127.6 billion against an estimate of US$128.2 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of US$2.67 missed the Wall Street target of US$3.02. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said AI-driven capital expenditures would increase significantly in 2027 and that near-term margin pressure was expected from third-party cloud capacity use.
items.title: Alphabet Shares Drop After Revenue Miss and Rising AI Cash Burn

items.summary: NVIDIA announced a conference call on Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss its third-quarter fiscal-year 2027 results, which ended October 25, 2026. The event will be webcast live in listen-only mode on investor.nvidia.com, with prepared remarks from CFO Colette Kress followed by a Q&A limited to financial analysts and institutional investors. Results are expected at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, ahead of which NVIDIA will post written commentary; the call will cover its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2027 results as well.
items.title: NVIDIA Schedules Conference Call for Third-Quarter Fiscal-Year Results

items.summary: Microsoft reported total revenue of $92.3bn and profit above $36.6bn for the September quarter, exceeding analyst estimates of around $90.6bn in revenue and $35.1bn in profit per FactSet. Growth was driven by Azure cloud computing, which rose 48%. The report followed voluntary buyouts offered to about 60,000 employees as Microsoft invests heavily in artificial intelligence.
items.title: Microsoft Beats Revenue Expectations Amid Employee Buyouts

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet missed Wall Street profit and revenue expectations, sending its shares down more than 10% in extended trading. The company reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion as AI spending accelerated its burn. Total revenue reached $127.6 billion against an estimate of $128.2 billion, while net income fell 25% to $26.17 billion and adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.67 versus a target of $3.02.
items.title: Alphabet shares drop over 10% after AI-driven earnings miss

items.summary: On its debut listing on Wednesday, Jio Platforms became the second most valued company in India and fifth most valued telecom services provider globally. It listed at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium over its IPO price of Rs 1,119, closing at Rs 1,419, up 27%. Late buying pushed late session market capitalisation to Rs 13. 1 lakh crore, behind Reliance Industries (Rs 15. 7 lakh crore) but ahead of Bharti Airtel (Rs 12. 2 lakh crore). The listing made RIL group the top business house at a combined Rs 30. 3 lakh crore, just past Tata group's Rs 25. 4 lakh crore.
items.title: Jio Platforms Debuts as India's Second Most Valued Company

items.summary: On Wednesday, Microsoft forecast fiscal second-quarter cloud growth and overall sales that beat Wall Street estimates, sending shares up more than 5 per cent in after-hours trading. The company reported $18.6 billion in first-quarter free cash flow — some $10 billion above expectations — as capital spending came in below its own projection of $50 billion and Azure surged 48 per cent. Microsoft expects second-quarter Azure growth of 49 to 50 per cent, ahead of analyst estimates of 47.6 per cent. The results contrast with Alphabet's negative cash flow and Meta's debt reliance, positioning Microsoft as a counterweight amid AI-spending anxiety.
items.title: Microsoft's Cloud Growth and Cash Flow Ease AI Spending Fears

items.summary: Bets in prediction markets are shaping how retail investors speculate about high-profile IPOs, including Anthropic's public offering. The AI lab filed for a listing that could value it between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. On Polymarket more than a dozen markets have formed around its fundraising, exchange and valuation; rival Kalshi is also attracting bets on the deal details. Michael Ashley Schulman of Cerity Partners likened the interest to crowds lining up for an iPhone release.
items.title: Prediction markets draw heavy bets on Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Alphabet's stock fell 7% in after-hours trading Wednesday as the company missed profit projections and raised its third-quarter AI spending past $50 billion. The cash burn intensified investor concerns that hyperscalers are not generating enough revenue to justify debt-funded infrastructure investments, while Microsoft shares rose on stronger cloud results.
items.title: Alphabet Stock Falls After Earnings Miss and Rising AI Spending

items.summary: For the first time, Microsoft reported Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion for the July-September quarter, up 48% from a year earlier. The disclosure lets investors compare it directly with Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, which already report cloud figures in dollars. Alphabet said Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion in the same quarter.
items.title: Microsoft Discloses Azure's First Dollar Revenue in a Record Quarter

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Amazon announced five new smart home devices, introducing two all-new categories: the $230 Alexa Photo Frame and the $200 Echo Time. Both are available now, alongside an upgraded $100 Echo Dot and a $250 Echo Studio with a built-in Home Camera. A redesigned $500 Echo Show 16 is available for preorder, shipping in mid-December. Amazon also announced Alexa Home Map, which creates interactive 3D maps of homes using compatible devices like Ring cameras and lidar-equipped smartphones. ZDNET raises privacy concerns about the feature's real-time surveillance capabilities.
items.title: Amazon Unveils Five New Smart Home Devices and Features

items.summary: For over a decade, Apple executives opposed touchscreens in Macs. Steve Jobs called them fatiguing in 2010; Craig Federighi and John Turnus echoed the view through 2021. Now Apple has unveiled a MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring a touchscreen, reversing its long-held position.
items.title: Apple Adds Touchscreen to MacBook Pro After Decades of Resistance

items.summary: The Korea Media and Communications Commission fined Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won on Wednesday, according to The Associated Press. The regulator said the companies misused their dominant app-store positions by forcing domestic developers onto proprietary billing and delaying approvals without clear explanations.
items.title: Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Payment Rules

items.summary: Apple announced a touchscreen MacBook Pro carrying a tandem OLED display it calls PROLED XDR, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, an in-panel touch sensor, Dynamic Island, a 12MP camera and macOS 27. The line comes in 14.2-inch and 16.3-inch sizes with entry prices of $2,899 for the 14-inch model with the M5 Pro chip and $4,799 for the 16-inch model with the M5 Max chip, according to Apple; all figures are U.S. starting prices. Touch models carry a $400 premium over equivalent non-touch versions, though Apple did not list those base prices. Preorders opened Oct. 28, 2026, with deliveries scheduled for Nov. 6, 2026.
items.title: Apple Unveils Touchscreen MacBook Pro at $2,899

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to appear in person on Wednesday over a contempt petition for remarks against Chief Justice Surya Kant and the judiciary. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi called the matter important as it concerns the entire institution of the judiciary. Journalist Nikhil Wagle, facing the same charge of scandalising the institution, was exempted from physical appearance and asked to appear virtually after being represented by a lawyer in court proceedings on Wednesday.
items.title: Supreme Court Summons Sanjay Raut in Contempt Case Over Judiciary Remarks

items.summary: A federal judge in San Jose, California, ordered the Trump administration to stop enforcing a Pentagon ban barring defense business with companies that lobby for Alibaba. The ruling tested Washington's ability to limit Chinese firms' activities but did not address Alibaba's separate challenge to its placement on the 1260H list added June 8. Bloomberg News reported the case as closely watched amid US-China rivalry.
items.title: Alibaba Wins Ruling on Lobbying Ban Tied to US Blacklisting

items.summary: A Tesla owner writing seven years after paying $6000 for a permanent Full Self-Driving subscription now drives a 2026 Model Y with FSD V14 and reports needing to intervene or complain only rarely. He lists improvements such as handling trip start and end, Automatic Collision Evasion that activates without engagement, recognizing flashing school-zone lights at 20 mph, navigating construction barrels, summoning in rain, crosswalk stops, deer braking, debris avoidance, lane discipline on four-lane freeways, removing the stop-sign pause after about 1.5 seconds, correct turn-lane selection and parking into garages or chosen spots. He calls FSD a safety feature that has saved lives but says Tesla is withholding it from customers who have not paid $99/month, noting he believes Automatic Collision Evasion could be offered to everyone without enabling autonomous driving. As of Q3 2026 he cites a 75% uptake rate for new buyers versus 12% previously, while estimating at least 15% still lack the feature.
items.title: Tesla Owner Credits FSD V14 With Fewer Interventions

items.summary: Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino said the Australian Taxation Office, led by commissioner Rob Heferen, could have done better on handling a complex problem when deciding how to address the ban on credit card payment surcharges. The tax office will extend accepting credit card payments until June 2026.
items.title: Mulino says ATO could have handled credit card ban better

items.summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro landed in Miami after losing the presidential runoff, denying he fled. He said leaving was for Brazil's sake and called himself a victim of persecution. His exit followed confusion over his whereabouts; Brazilian police cancelled his passports on Tuesday after he missed a 24-hour surrender deadline. Flight tracking placed him at Puerto Iguazú before reaching Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport just before 09:30 local time (13:30 GMT). He faces two Supreme Federal Court investigations, one involving nearly $70m (£53m) transferred to a film about his father. His parliamentary immunity ends on 31 January.
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Denies Fleeing Brazil After Landing in Miami

items.summary: An investigation by Dutch nonprofit Global Rights Compliance revealed new details about a Russian labor-brokering platform that employs North Korean workers in violation of international law, benefiting Moscow's war effort in Ukraine. The report, released Thursday, examines Vladimir Sokolov, who directs the Black Horse group and KNDR.su, an online platform sourcing North Korean workers for Russian employers.
items.title: Dutch nonprofit exposes Russian platform hiring North Korean workers illegally

items.summary: Political action committees funded by technology companies, utilities and other corporate interests have spent nearly twice as much backing Proposition 45 as public interest and labor groups opposing it. The measure would rewrite the California Environmental Quality Act, which requires agencies to disclose a project's environmental impacts, shifting who sets review scope from public agencies to developers. Supporters say it modernizes approvals while keeping protections; critics call it a smokescreen that gutts community input. A nonpartisan office estimates Prop 45 could cost state and local governments $100 million or more yearly. Recent polling shows voter opposition has fallen sharply, though the measure still faces an uncertain vote on Nov. 3.
items.title: Corporate PACs Bankroll Effort to Weaken California's CEQA Law

items.summary: Microsoft reported a 32% profit rise in its third quarter, the company said, even as it increased spending sharply. On Oct 28, Microsoft disclosed US$45.2 billion (S$57.9 billion) in capital expenditures for the three months ending September, up about 30% from $34.9 billion a year earlier. Revenue was US$92.3 billion, up 19%, and profit reached US$36.6 billion. The results beat Wall Street expectations and contrasted with weaker reports from Meta and Alphabet. CEO Satya Nadella noted the company added 24 data centres across five continents amid rising demand. Microsoft also offered buyouts to about 60,000 workers in four countries, roughly a quarter of its workforce of about 223,000.
items.title: Microsoft Posts Profit Jump on AI Spending

items.summary: Billionaire Gautam Adani is exploring a potential acquisition of Dutch energy storage group VTTI as supply disruptions make its facilities more valuable for trading, people familiar with the matter said. A deal could value VTTI at around €3 billion ($3.4 billion), they said. Deliberations are ongoing and there’s no certainty they’ll result in a transaction; IFM, Adnoc and VTTI declined to comment.
items.title: Adani Explores €3 Billion VTTI Energy Storage Deal

items.summary: On Wednesday, Alphabet missed Wall Street profit and revenue expectations while accelerated AI spending worsened its cash burn, sending shares down more than 10 per cent in extended trading. The company reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion versus near breakeven estimates, a loss driven by AI research costs. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said capex would rise significantly in 2027 and warned of margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity.
items.title: Alphabet Shares Fall After Revenue Miss and Rising AI Cash Burn

items.summary: Amazon announced a second round of job cuts this month, eliminating no more than 250 software development jobs. A spokesperson said the move would help Amazon operate more efficiently and align with its product roadmap. The company had already cut about 16,000 jobs in January and 14,000 employees in October 2025. Across tech, TrueUp reports 670 companies announced layoffs this year.
items.title: Amazon cuts up to 250 software roles amid tech layoffs

items.summary: Alphabet reported $127. 6 billion in revenue, up 25% year over year during its third-quarter earnings call Wednesday. Google announced it is expanding ads in AI mode into international markets for the first time globally, alongside multi-turn and conversational discovery formats built on Gemini-powered features introduced in May. Philipp Schindler said click-through rates are already comparable to organic listings. Search advertising growth decelerated to 12% from 17%, putting pressure on monetizing AI features as Alphabet shares fell 8%. Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30. 7 billion, while the Services division generated $96. 3 billion, up 11%.
items.title: Google Expands AI Search Ads Globally Amid Slowing Core Ad Growth

items.summary: A ZDNET reviewer, searching for a frame for his dining room or kitchen, says the new 10-inch HD Alexa Photo Frame could work. It includes Alexa+, which uses AI to choose photos based on people, seasons and smiles, plus voice notes attached to images. The device pulls pictures directly from Amazon Photos and is available now starting at $200 or $230 in walnut or birch finishes.
items.title: Reviewer Finds Amazon's Alexa Photo Frame Could Fit His Home

items.summary: The Supreme Court said it had not yet examined the legality of the 'logical discrepancy' criterion used to delete voters during the 2003-based voter enumeration exercise, even though validity of the Bihar exercise was upheld. The bench questioned whether the Election Commission could reopen entries beyond the base list and asked for additional filters before deciding later in the case brought by opposition INDIA bloc functionaries led by Rahul Gandhi; earlier it had found nothing amiss in SIR's conduct or proportionality under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.},
items.title: Supreme Court Defers on Logical Discrepancy Legality in SIR Case

items.summary: Patrick Tan Siong Kuan argues that as Singapore approaches its 60th year of national service, the country should reconsider enlisting women amid a fast-declining birth rate and ageing population. He notes then Defence Minister Ng Eng Hen's May 2022 concern about societal costs outweighing benefits, but suggests a shorter one-month training course with a reduced 12-month service period could be considered, or that Singaporeans decide via survey or referendum.
items.title: Singapore MP Calls for Reconsideration of Women in National Service

items.summary: Apple introduced a new 24-inch iMac and an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, both powered by the M6 chip that first appeared in the Mac mini. The updates focus on internal changes rather than appearance. Apple said the M6 makes the iMac five times faster for artificial intelligence compared with the 2024 model, while the new MacBook Pro is 30% faster in graphics. Both machines start at $1,499 and $1,999 respectively.
items.title: Apple Unveils M6 iMac and Entry MacBook Pro

items.summary: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers, describing it as its first real-time world model to generate audio natively. The system builds explorable worlds from text and image prompts in real time, producing visuals plus ambient noise, music and character dialogue together. A Gemini model now runs inside the simulation loop as a planner that interprets input, breaks goals into steps, verifies frames and replans when needed. DeepMind states it ran internal safety evaluations before the preview. The team frames the design as an early step toward hybrid world models for agent or robot training environments. TechCrunch’s briefing notes scene consistency of up to 2 minutes, double Genie 3, while sessions reportedly last only a few minutes and objects drift after repeated prompt edits. DeepMind lists open problems including visual detail drift in longer sessions, limited interaction length, imperfect real-world location accuracy and unsolved audio accuracy for multi-agent interactions.
items.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Genie 4 Real-Time World Model With Native Audio

items.summary: More than 41,000 US Department of Homeland Security personnel details were leaked Wednesday by the group Department of Peace and researcher maia crimew through a database called Icepick. The leak lists names, work addresses and phone numbers for thousands of immigration-enforcement agents across Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement. A DHS representative did not respond to comment requests as public backlash grows over rising arrests and deportations under the Trump Administration.
items.title: Leaked DHS Immigration Agent Records Draw Backlash Amid Deportation Push

items.summary: An eight-year-old girl was seriously injured, suffering head injuries, in a wolf attack inside an enclosure at the Johannismühle wildlife park near Baruth/Mark, south of Berlin. Police said she was with a staff member and two other children when it happened before opening at 10:00 local time (09:00 GMT). She was flown to hospital by helicopter; no one else was hurt. The park is temporarily closed and set to reopen on 2 November, the incident coming after recent animal attacks across Europe.
items.title: Eight-Year-Old Girl Seriously Injured in Wolf Attack at German Wildlife Park

items.summary:
On 28th October 2026, Ted Sanders explained how OpenAI orders its models by size: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra. He said LLM performance is multidimensional but largely driven by model size, which affects reliability, cost per token and recall of esoteric facts. Version numbers signal release order, relationship to other releases and magnitude of improvement; for example 6.1 launched after 5.6 without the jump of a version 7 (quoted in the item). He noted no guarantee that the best model at math is also strongest at jokes.

visual null
items.title: Ted Sanders Explains OpenAI's Model Naming Conventions

items.summary: Brazilian political candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.
items.title: Defeated Flavio Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami Amid Investigations

items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh kept the central bank on track for another rate increase this year, even while declining to give explicit guidance on policy. Citing a strong economy and ongoing inflation concerns, he reinforced expectations of December hikes with possible further increases in early 2027. Vincent Reinhart of BNY Investments noted that Warsh was signaling more tightening while leaving room for it to be modest.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates as Warsh Signals More Hikes Ahead

items.summary: The Netherlands pledged $500 million over 10 years to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, boosting long-term tropical forest conservation. The fund aims toward a $125 billion endowment; current pledges total roughly $7.8 billion. Environmental economist Bard Harstad criticized its economic solvency and noted governments may reverse commitments if leaders like Bolsonaro return to power. Conservationists praised it as a major breakthrough for global forest protection.
items.title: Netherlands Pledges $500 Million for Tropical Forest Conservation Fund

items.summary: New World screwworm, a deadly parasite whose larvae burrow into animal wounds, was found in Arizona for the first time after being detected in a dog in Cochise County. The US Department of Agriculture confirmed the infection late Wednesday. Total cases since June reached 71, with 18 active and 10 located in New Mexico as infections accelerated this month.
items.title: Screwworm Detected in Arizona for First Time as Outbreak Accelerates

items.summary: Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro landed in Miami with his family on Wednesday and declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil. He had not conceded Sunday's election to President Luiz Inacio da Silva (Lula), alleging irregularities. The Brazilian electoral authority said Wednesday that voting proceeded normally, while international observers called it fair. Bolsonaro faces criminal investigations before the Supreme Court but frames them as a political witch hunt by left-leaning justices.
items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami, Calls Himself Brazil's Leader

items.summary: Spain's transport minister says a Wednesday rail collision in Castilla-La Mancha that killed at least 68 people followed an order to run despite a technical failure. The findings may revive safety questions after a January high-speed crash killed 46.
items.title: Spanish Transport Minister Says Rail Crash Followed Faulty 'Error' Order

items.summary: Snapper fishing could resume across much of South Australia from July under the state government's Snapper Rebuilding Plan. SARDI research shows stocks have replenished to more than 20 per cent on the West Coast, Spencer Gulf and Gulf St Vincent after a closure that began in 2019. The ban was extended 12 months due to an algal bloom. Easing depends on summer assessments confirming biomass over 20 per cent with sufficient recruitment. Fishers raised concerns about catch allocations, data collection limits and past management.
items.title: South Australia Aims to Reopen Snapper Fishery After Eight-Year Ban

items.summary: Questions are being raised about Spain's rail safety after authorities launched an official investigation into Wednesday's high-speed train collision, which killed at least 68 people and wounded around 100 more. It was the country's second fatal rail crash this year and Europe's deadliest since 2013. Transport minister Oscar Puente said a red signal triggered by a computer communications failure led to an erroneous decision to restart the Renfe train, which then struck the stationary Iryo service. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez declared all of Spain in mourning and vowed to strengthen safety if needed. The January accident on the same line killed 46 people; a preliminary Civil Guard report cited track defects as its leading theory. Railway safety authority data showed accidents rose from 45 in 2016 to 69 last year, while passenger numbers fell about 14% in early 2026 amid ongoing maintenance-spending concerns.
items.title: Spain Launches Probe After Second Fatal High-Speed Train Crash in a Year

items.summary: Treasury measures announced in the Budget should make more than 100 products cheaper, saving a typical household about £21 a year on food. Restaurant owners question how much it helps them, wanting VAT cuts or staff-cost relief instead. Morgan Austin of Burgerism said rising minimum wage and National Insurance costs hit her business hard, costing about £150,000 a year. Hassan Zahid of Fuego 1987 called the impact minor, while Gavin Williams of Mattina coffee shop in Salford said it would make zero difference because his suppliers are UK-based.
items.title: Restaurant owners doubt food tariff savings

items.summary: Rescuers worked overnight near Urda, using cranes to lift wreckage from mangled carriages at the site of a collision between two high-speed trains. The disaster killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100 on 28 October, making it Spain's second deadly rail collision this year. In Madrid, dozens held a minute of silence in Cibeles Square; opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo attended as the gathering turned into a protest calling for Transport Minister Óscar Puente to resign.
items.title: Madrid mourns and protests after deadly Spanish train crash

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey raised taxes on banks and landlords in his first budget to fund a £100 winter handout sent to 20 million English households in council tax bands A-D. The £2.6bn cost includes funding for Scottish and Welsh governments, which he hoped would run similar schemes. He blamed global economic storms, including the war in Iran driving up oil and gas prices, for a grim outlook. Critics argued the support was poorly targeted while savers faced higher taxes and rents could rise. Meanwhile, official forecasts warned of virtually no growth in disposable income by 2030-31 as inflation rises to almost 4%. Bond markets remained unruffled despite higher-than-expected borrowing against Labour's fiscal rules.
items.title: Healey's Budget Taxes Banks and Landlords for Winter Handout

items.summary: Western Australia's electric vehicle charging network, launched in 2015, is aging and facing maintenance problems. The Shire of Harvey may pay up to $120,000 to replace its only station. Energy Minister Amber-Jade Sanderson says local governments and the private sector must support it after RAC withdrew last year. Licensed EVs rose from 150 in 2015 to more than 60,000 by June this year.
items.title: WA councils left to fund aging EV chargers

items.summary:
The Office for Budget Responsibility's latest forecast flags soaring energy prices as the biggest near-term risk to the UK economy, cutting its growth prediction for next year from 1.6% to 1%. The OBR expects inflation to peak at 3.8% in 2027 and average 3.4% next year before easing toward the Bank of England's 2% target. Chancellor John Healey announced policies offering households "breathing space," while economist David Miles called it a "grim" period with "virtually no growth." Pantheon Macroeconomics described government support as "small beer given the surge in inflation we expect over the winter." The OBR noted "significant uncertainty" amid Middle East conflict. Interest rates, currently 3.75%, could rise to 4.5% in coming years.

visual null},
items.title: OBR Warns UK Economy Faces Energy-Driven Inflation and Stalled Growth

items.summary: A Grand Canyon Trust analysis of groundwater sampling spanning 32 years across 40 sites finds that three of four wells with arsenic above the EPA drinking-water standard are at the Pinyon Plain uranium mine. The monitoring well exceeded permitted alert levels for arsenic four times since 2025, and sump water reached over 3,000 times the safe limit. Havasupai Tribal Chairwoman Melinda Yaiva framed opposition as a duty to protect her people's water. Energy Fuels Resources Inc.'s Misael Cabrera said mineral deposits are natural; ADEQ and the company attribute rising arsenic to groundwater pumping causing a cone of depression, a claim critics dispute pending more data.
items.title: Grand Canyon Uranium Mine Arsenic Analysis Points to Contamination Source

items.summary: Protests are spreading across Europe, from France and Italy to Albania, with clashes between demonstrators and police raising questions about the causes of public discontent. On an episode of The Point, experts Rong Ying, Fabien Pacory and Remi Piet examine the forces behind the unrest and what it means for European governments.
items.title: European Protests Sweep From France To Italy And Albania Amid Clashes With Police

items.summary: China now supplies nearly 70% of global electrolyzer manufacturing capacity, exporting machines at roughly 60% lower stack costs than Western alternatives. Analysts note the country's surplus production and Five-Year Plan push toward green hydrogen demand, though system-level cost gaps remain as Western markets resist dependence.
items.title: China Builds Global Electrolyzer Industry While West Lags

items.summary: Prediction market Kalshi hired political strategist Eric Schultz as an out-of-house adviser, a person familiar with the matter told Semafor. The hiring arrives amid Democratic forecasts in Tuesday’s midterms: Kalshi users put odds at 91% for a House majority and 65% for a Senate majority. Kalshi declined to comment.
items.title: Kalshi hires Obama adviser Eric Schultz

items.summary: Drik Panchang lists Dhanteras for Friday, November 6, 2026, marking the opening of Diwali. For New Delhi it gives a puja muhurat from 6:02pm to 7:57pm IST and notes that Trayodashi spans two civil dates on the same day. The piece frames these as location-specific timings rather than nationwide, describes associated worship and purchases, and points readers to BIS hallmarking guidance for gold jewellery.
items.title: Dhanteras 2026 Date, Timings and Traditions Explained

items.summary: Arab parties in Israel's election appear poised for a record number of seats, with the two main blocs on track for around 19 Knesset seats. Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said his party would seek to use its projected 12 seats to help remove Netanyahu's government but could not join an Eisenkot-led coalition over Gaza and Lebanon policy. Ra'am chief Mansour Abbas expressed willingness to support such a minority govt from outside, while Likud spokesman Guy Levy dismissed any Arab cooperation as 'Not a chance.' The parties cite community protection demands amid ongoing negotiations with the change bloc.
items.title: Israel Arab Parties Position Themselves as Potential Kingmakers

items.summary: An MIT Technology Review Insights poll reports that fewer than one in five (16%) surveyed organizations are extracting transformative value from their AI deployments. The largest group, 40%, sees moderate gains, while 23% report minimal or no returns. Atlan co-founder Prukalpa Sankar says a missing context layer limits real usefulness inside companies.
items.title: MIT Technology Review poll finds few organizations extract transformative value from AI

items.summary: Rescue teams worked overnight near Urda, using cranes to lift wreckage from two high-speed trains that collided on 28 October. The accident is Spain's second deadly rail collision this year and one of Europe's deadliest railway accidents of the century. In Madrid, dozens gathered in Cibeles Square for a minute of silence organised by the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces, attended by opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo and Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida. The gathering turned into a protest against Transport Minister Óscar Puente, with participants holding placards reading 'Corruption kills' and chanting for his resignation.
items.title: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night

items.summary: The UN General Assembly again called to end the US embargo on Cuba, but support fell to its lowest level in more than 30 years. The resolution passed with 130 countries in favour, 17 against and 25 abstentions—the fewest backing since 1995. Germany, Italy and Latvia abstained for the first time in 34 years, while several nations voted against it.
items.title: UN Vote Support for Ending US Cuba Embargo Hits 30-Year Low

items.summary: José Luis Centella, president of the Communist Party of Spain, discusses how the Communist Party of China has sustained a century-long commitment to long-term planning, innovation-driven growth, and discipline. He offers his perspective on what enables this enduring capacity for reform, though he does not present these views as established fact but rather as an interpretation worth considering.
items.title: Centella on China's Communist Party and its reform drive

items.summary: Middle East nations renewed diplomatic efforts, with delegations from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan meeting Iranian officials in Tehran to explore a regional security framework. Standard Chartered expects an agreement could quickly reduce the geopolitical risk premium on oil, though prices will stay high until shipping lanes are secure and Gulf supply is reliable again. The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve holds just 282.7 million barrels, its lowest level since 1982, per EIA figures. Standard Chartered says crude prices remain elevated over the coming months as disrupted production and costly shipping limit effective supply. On natural gas, TTF traded at €98.58/MWh on Wednesday amid seasonal tightening.
items.title: Oil Buyers Face $100-Plus Prices Despite Middle East Peace Talks

items.summary: Dutch startup Elysian Aircraft says all-electric flight may be nearer if its E9X airliner succeeds, promising quieter flights and lower oil dependence. The aircraft is designed to carry up to 100 passengers about 1,000 km (620 miles), which the company claims could handle nearly 50% of scheduled commercial passenger flights worldwide and cut total aerospace emissions by 20% when it enters service in 2034. Daniel Jacobson, co-founder, told EuroNews that zero-emission transport over half the world's flights would reduce overall aviation emissions by a fifth.
items.title: Elysian Aircraft Targets Zero-Emission Short-Haul Flights

items.summary: Punjab Jail Minister Ravjot Singh inaugurated the Women's Open Air Jail at Central Jail Patiala on Wednesday during the Ujala Punjab Prison Olympics 2026. The event included tug-of-war, kabaddi and Giddha performances to promote inmate fitness and reintegration into society.
items.title: Punjab Jail Minister Inaugurates Women's Open Air Jail in Patiala

items.summary: On November 3, US citizens vote in midterm elections held at the halfway point of a presidential term. Voters choose representatives for all 435 House seats, some senators (35 this year), governors in 36 states, and members of state legislatures on issues from abortion to education. Analyst J. Miles Coleman notes midterms are often "a referendum on the president," especially given Trump's record-low approval ratings. Republicans currently hold slim majorities in both chambers; Democrats need only four more House seats (218) for control and four Senate seats overall, with Texas a key race. Because most federal decisions require congressional approval, these results would significantly affect how easily Trump can govern.
items.title: US midterms could shift Congress and reshape Trump's agenda

items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported operating profit of 107.4 trillion won for the July-to-October quarter, in line with its estimate and up from 12.2 trillion won a year earlier, driven by strong demand for AI chips. Shares rose as SK Hynix's upbeat outlook eased concerns about fading AI earnings momentum.
items.title: Samsung Posts Record Q3 Profit on AI Chip Demand

items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.04 billion) for the July-to-September quarter, nearly nine times the year earlier figure of 12.2 trillion won, matching its own estimate. The gain reflects strong AI chip demand, though investors remain cautious about whether spending will hold.
items.title: Samsung Posts Record Q3 Profit on AI Chip Demand

items.summary: Treasury bill cutoff yields rose about 20 basis points above the previous auction, reaching their highest level in nearly two years. Traders attributed this to near deficit liquidity and elevated crude prices driving a higher liquidity premium. The 91-day yield came in at 5.93%, while longer tenures reached 6.54% for 182 days and 6.69% for 364 days, per RBI data.
items.title: RBI Treasury Bill Yields Reach Two-Year High Amid Liquidity Tightening and Oil Prices

items.summary: Apple claims its new M6-powered MacBook Pro delivers up to 13 times faster first-token performance for LLM prompts than the older M1 model, and promises up to 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch OLED display reaches 1,600 nits with a 120Hz refresh rate. Launched in India on October 27, it starts at ₹2,39,900, with upgrades pushing the final price higher. Pre-orders are open and Indian sales begin November 6.
items.title: Apple's OLED MacBook Pro 2026 carries a costly price catch

items.summary: BYD now employs more than 1.02 million people, according to chairman Wang Chuanfu, who shared the figures at the China Society of Automotive Engineers' 33rd annual conference on Wednesday. The headcount exceeds the combined workforce of Toyota, GM, Ford and Tesla by roughly 170,000. BYD reached this level after a hiring surge in late 2025 following an earlier cut to about 869,600 employees at year-end 2025. The article notes that most workers are based in China while sales grow overseas, and cautions that the large headcount reflects vertical integration rather than output alone: BYD produces roughly 5.3 vehicles per worker versus around 12 to 29 for its rivals.
items.title: BYD Surpasses Toyota, GM, Ford and Tesla in Total Workforce

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet reported disappointing third-quarter results, sending its shares down about 10 per cent after hours. Total revenue of $127.6 billion missed estimates, driven by a $1.4-billion shortfall in advertising that offset gains from Google Cloud revenues more than doubling to $30.71 billion. The company posted negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion and burned $5.9 billion last quarter, the first loss in 22 years as a public company. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said she expected near-term margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity. Investors also worried about higher 2027 capital spending forecasts of $205 billion versus this year's $195 billion. Analysts questioned whether Google rushed AI model deployment amid softer financial metrics.
items.title: Alphabet shares fall as search miss and AI cash burn weigh on results

items.summary: Microsoft shares rose more than five percent Wednesday after the company reported total revenue of $92.3 billion and profit of more than $36.6 billion, figures it attributed to its Azure cloud division growing 48 percent in the September quarter. Analysts had expected around $90.6 billion in revenue and $35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.
items.title: Microsoft Shares Rise on Strong Azure Growth and Quarterly Earnings

items.summary: Microsoft reported $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments and Azure services, for the quarter ended September 30, per a regulatory filing. That figure represents nearly 11% of Microsoft's total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion. For fiscal year 2026, OpenAI-related revenue reached $24.1 billion.
items.title: Microsoft Reports $10 Billion in OpenAI Revenue for Quarter

items.summary: Microsoft reported a record quarter with revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19% over the year-ago period, marking its tenth consecutive quarterly record. Net income on a GAAP basis reached $36.6 billion, up 32%. Cloud drove growth to $63.9 billion, led by Azure at $33.2 billion and OpenAI revenue of $10 billion. Microsoft also noted capital expenditures topped $45.2 billion, another record.
items.title: Microsoft Posts Tenth Straight Quarter of Record Revenue

items.summary: Procore, a global construction management software provider serving tens of thousands of customers across the U.S., Europe, Middle East, Asia, and Australia, has built Procore Analytics 2.0 on a medallion architecture inside Databricks using OpenSharing to deliver governed data extracts into customer tools like Power BI, Tableau, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and SQL Server. The upgrade replaced the older API-based system that capped refreshes at three times daily. Procore reports Analytics 2.0 expanded its table catalog from several years of work in version 1.0 to hundreds of tables in under half the time, effectively doubling extractable data surface area. Matthew Guptill, Product Manager for Procore Analytics, said OpenSharing has increased visibility across construction teams and helped deliver projects on time, budget, and safely.
items.title: Procore Builds OpenSharing Data Platform for Construction Analytics

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Anthropic has made three beta features generally available for Claude Enterprise plans: smart reports, pooled budgets, and in-app surveys. These tools track task usage, costs, friction points, and workflow opportunities while setting monthly spend caps per group and seat. The move comes as Anthropic faces scrutiny ahead of its IPO amid concerns about enterprise AI spending.
items.title: Anthropic Rolls Out AI ROI Tracking Tools for Enterprise Clients

items.summary: Amazon announced the new Echo Show 16, a 16-inch smart display with integrated Fire TV. The standard model starts at $500; the Nanomatte version costs $570. Amazon said its wide-angle camera doubles Visual ID range to 17 feet and the device has 20% more computing power than the Echo Show 15, which it claims is nearly 40% thinner with twice as vibrant colors.
items.title: Amazon debuts Echo Show 16, a large smart display with Fire TV

items.summary: Several mutual fund houses have temporarily halted fresh investments in Gold Funds of Funds since mid-October, affecting lump-sum purchases, new SIP registrations and switch-ins. The Economic Times explains that investors can instead consider Gold ETFs, which remain open to new investment despite the FoF restrictions.
items.title: Gold FoFs Face Fresh Investment Restrictions Amid Market Uncertainty

items.summary: Wednesday, Jio Platforms listed on the National Stock Exchange as the 3,138th company following India's largest public offering. A listing pop of 21.36% made it the second most valuable Indian company by market cap, while parent Reliance Industries Group became the country's largest conglomerate, surpassing Tata Group. Patriarch Mukesh Ambani showed emotion as his children spoke at the bell-ringing ceremony attended by four generations.
items.title: Jio Platforms Lists on NSE as Ambani Family Celebrates Milestone

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi mocked the Congress party on X Wednesday, asking how many seats it won in Legislative Council elections across four states. The opposition secured none of the 28 ballot-paper seats.
items.title: Modi mocks Congress over MLC election rout

items.summary: At the Jio Platforms IPO listing ceremony in Mumbai, Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani was visibly moved and wiped tears from his eyes while listening to speeches by his children Anant and Isha Ambani. The next-generation executives reflected on the company's growth, family vision, and societal reach of Jio.
items.title: Reliance Chairman Wipes Tears at Jio IPO Ceremony

items.summary: In Gaza and the West Bank, many Palestinians focus less on Israel's election result than on whether it would bring real change. Whether Benjamin Netanyahu stays in power with his far-right allies or centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot wins, few expect hope from Tuesday's vote. Huda al-Houli, a displaced resident of Khan Younis, said they fear the elections could bring an even worse leader.
items.title: Palestinians See Little Hope in Israeli Election Outcome

items.summary: The New South Wales parliament passed legislation creating the Great Koala National Park, which campaigners called a historic win after more than a decade of campaigning. The park will span 475,000 hectares (1.2 million acres), incorporating 178,000 hectares (440,000 acres) of state forests and other government land into the national estate before opening by end of 2026. Long-term funding relies on Australian Carbon Credit Units under the Improved Native Forest Management method, an approach critics say risks greenwashing conservation. Multiple attempts to amend the scheme were voted down in parliament.
items.title: NSW Approves Great Koala National Park on Carbon-Funded Terms

items.summary: In Tokyo, Ryua moved into a rental apartment after seeing a man glare at her during a viewing; since the agent could not see him, she concluded he was a ghost and chose to stay. She reports daily paranormal activity four years later. The property carries a roughly 30% rent discount on its small bedsit in Setagaya. Diane Tincher, an American living in rural Kagoshima for nearly 40 years, bought a three-bedroom house for about half the usual price after an elderly woman died alone there. She researched it via Oshimaland, a crowdsourced site listing stigmatised properties launched in 2005 and expanded internationally by 2011. Founder Teru Oshima notes such homes were once unattractive options; a 2025 survey found more than half of Japanese people would now rent one if cheap.
items.title: Japan's haunted homes draw bargain hunters amid rising prices

items.summary: Japan and the US agreed Wednesday (Oct 28) to set up a Japanese facility for jointly producing advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles used by F-35 fighter jets, according to Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. The announcement came during his meeting with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Cebu, Philippines. Koizumi called the project part of “Operation Supercharge” and said the missiles are essential for the F-35 but gave no further details.
items.title: US and Japan Agree on Missile Production Facility in Cebu

items.summary: Persistent Systems could raise around Rs 6,000 crore through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to fund its acquisition of Nagarro. The debt would replace an 18-month bridge loan from Barclays and match the company's cash flows over tenures up to five years with an average maturity of about three years. Persistent had earlier raised Rs 4,264 crore via a QIP.
items.title: Persistent Systems Plans Rs 6,000 Crore Debt Raise for Nagarro Acquisition

items.summary: Canada and the European Union agreed in a joint declaration to pursue closer ties but dropped a proposal for associate EU membership ahead of a Montreal summit. Prime Minister Mark Carney aims to reduce Canada's reliance on the US amid Trump tariffs, though critics warn the move risks angering Washington.
items.title: Canada and EU Drop Associate Membership Plan Amid Trade Tensions

items.summary: Petrol and diesel prices stayed unchanged across several Indian cities on October 29, while CNG rose in many locations. Chennai, Mathura and Meerut saw ₹2 increases; Mumbai, Bengaluru and Sonipat added ₹1 each; Bharatpur, Dewas and Firozabad recorded rises of 50 paise. Hyderabad had the highest petrol price at ₹116.15, while Chandigarh was lowest at ₹101.54. Diesel ranged from ₹89.47 in Chandigarh to ₹104.40 in Thiruvananthapuram. CNG climbed across several cities but stayed unchanged in New Delhi, Hyderabad, Rewari and NCR. Prices were taken from Goodreturns by LiveMint's Sounak Mukhopadhyay.
items.title: Indian Fuel Prices Steady as CNG Rises in Many Cities

items.summary: Muamer Nukic, a 51-year-old Protective Services Group employee with Queensland Police, pleaded guilty to making nine offensive and antisemitic comments on Threads. The court found that in the post he advocated for violence and rape. He was sentenced to a nine-month good-behaviour bond and fined $1,000.
items.title: Queensland Police Employee Fined Over Antisemitic Social Media Comments

items.summary: A report merged Thursday claimed at least three documents among the released Jeffrey Epstein files indicate that classified information was included, though what exactly was classified remains unclear. CBC News reported one document shows the Office of the Deputy Attorney General received classified material related to Epstein in March 2025. The DOJ has maintained the files contain no national security secrets and says it collected about 6 million pages but released over 3 million after review. CBS News analysis found tens of thousands of missing pages, including around 1.2 million gaps in one sequence, suggesting documents were removed without clear reason.
items.title: Report flags gaps and classified clues in Epstein file release

items.summary: Finshots examined Swiggy's second-quarter FY27 results and questioned whether its quick-commerce arm, Instamart, is outpacing the food delivery business. Adjusted revenue rose 34% to ₹7,909 crore while adjusted EBITDA reached ₹341 crore. However, Instamart's adjusted loss widened to ₹895 crore as Swiggy added 69 net dark stores and spent on pricing initiatives like the ₹9 Store. The outlet noted that growth may not yet justify costs and compared Instamart against Blinkit, suggesting profitability depends on scale. Swiggy reported a closing cash balance of ₹13,662 crore to fund expansion.
items.title: Swiggy's Instamart Losses Widened as Quick Commerce Investment Grows

items.summary: Craig Winder, director of Victoria Crime News and a home security business, admitted his credited local reporters do not exist; workers in the Philippines write stories attributed to fictitious Australian journalists. ABC NEWS Verify reported VCN has filed over 250 articles since February 2026 while crediting a four-person team, and that AI chatbots recommend it as reliable despite glaring errors and AI-generated images. Momoko Fujita of the University of Canberra called it 'pink slime' journalism. Winder said he set up the site to raise awareness of crime in his state and compel government action, but conceded using fake bios was somewhat deceptive.
items.title: Victoria crime news site owner admits using Filipino writers

items.summary: India's Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls has drawn concern over the possible disenfranchisement of eligible voters and its resemblance to a citizenship test. The revision, begun in Bihar in June 2025, presumes eligibility only from two-decade-old rolls, so most people under about 40 must link through a parent or grandparent or produce documents. In 2025 the Association for Democratic Reforms challenged it in the Supreme Court; on May 27 the court allowed limited enquiry into citizenship but left how to conduct it unclear. By September 1, draft rolls were missing 13.37 crore names. Veena Naregal of the Institute of Economic Growth argues a method refined over welfare schemes has now reached every voter.
items.title: Supreme Court Clears Path for Citizenship Checks in Voter Roll Revision

items.summary: A high-speed train collision killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more on Wednesday morning around 140km south of Madrid, between Mora and Orgaz. The Renfe-operated train was struck from behind by an Iryo train that had stopped for a computer failure; several carriages fell down an embankment. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the crash followed a system failure and human error in Madrid's control centre, calling it one of Europe's worst disasters and Spain's deadliest since 2013. Survivors described passengers thrown into the air, fire and dead bodies. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called for an investigation amid national grief.
items.title: Spain's deadliest train crash in over a decade kills at least 68

items.summary: KPMG's 2026 India CEO Outlook reports that 87% of Indian chief executive officers are confident about their organisations' growth prospects over the next three years, up from 83% in 2025. Confidence in India's broader growth stands at 73%, compared with 71% a year earlier. The survey raises questions about whether this optimism will translate into faster investment, stronger earnings and sustained hiring amid geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty and technological disruption.
items.title: Indian CEOs Expect Growth Despite Uncertainty, KPMG Survey Finds

items.summary: Two high-speed passenger trains travelling from Madrid to Seville collided in Spain, the item reports. A computer failure in the automatic signalling system had halted all trains on a stretch of line. Passengers say one train was then ordered to proceed and crashed into the rear of the other between Mora and Orgaz, about 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid. Survivors described carriages destroyed, debris everywhere and people thrown from their seats; some were trapped or injured. Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente called it 'truly unbelievable'. The accident has raised questions for authorities amid the country's recent rail safety concerns after 46 deaths in January at Adamuz near Córdoba. Affected passengers expressed anger that no warning had been given to the driver of the second train.
items.title: Spanish rail collision after trains wrongly cleared to proceed

items.summary: Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara alleged that Ryanair staff threatened and discriminated against his family at a Dublin airport, posting the account on X. Describing it as shocking and his first unpleasant experience in Ireland, he exchanged messages with Sanjiva Weerawarana about discrimination abroad. At writing, Ryanair had not responded to his claims.
items.title: Sangakkara Alleges Discrimination by Ryanair Staff in Dublin

items.summary:
The Supreme Court directed the Election Commission of India not to force nearly 4.3 million Delhi voters removed from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) to reapply via Form 6, suggesting they instead use Form 8 or enumeration processes if on the 2026 roll. The bench urged officials to proactively reach out rather than burdening migrants who move frequently. It questioned whether algorithm-driven 'logical discrepancy' classifications involved meaningful human review and noted the category disenfranchised 2.71 million people in West Bengal, where it remains an interim arrangement only. The court set a two-week deadline for ECI to respond before rehearing the matter on October 30.

visual null
items.title: Supreme Court Questions Election Commission Over Voter Disenfranchisement Notices

items.summary: European news sites report that the last new Polestar 2 has rolled off Luqiao assembly line in China, with more than 200,000 of the all-electric sedan/hatchbacks built since its 2020 launch. The company has not confirmed this officially, but it aligns with plans for an updated Polestar 2 in 2027 and a new Polestar 7 SUV by early 2028. Production ends as Polestar exits the US after the Trump Administration's Commerce Department declined authorization under the Connected Vehicle Rule earlier this year. The article then turns to EV deals, noting discounts on the Polestar 3 and 4 in the US market before promoting a solar installer service. (59 words)
items.title: Polestar Ends Polestar 2 Production After China Plant Closes

items.summary: A fire gutted several shops at the Vasco Sunday Market in Goa late Wednesday night, starting near Tilak Maidan. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant visited the site with MLAs and assured government support for those affected. He said administrative staff were working to control the blaze while more details on its cause remain awaited.
items.title: Goa Chief Minister Assures Support After Vasco Sunday Market Fire Damages Shops

items.summary: Twenty-seven years after the 1999 Staines murders in Manoharpur, Odisha, a community lives in fear that convict Dara Singh's release could embolden extremist elements as attacks on churches intensify. The Odisha government told the Supreme Court on September 17 it opposes his release for now, citing concerns over communal tensions after about 200–250 Dara Sena members gathered outside Keonjhar jail on August 15, 2026. Witness Samson Marandi warned that harmony is 'certain to be under threat.' Church leader Jagat Ranjan Santra blamed the government's stance on political calculations and pointed to a surge in violence since the BJP came to power in 2024, including an incident where pastor Bipin Bihari Naik was assaulted. While Dara Sena member Ranjan Kumar Sahoo expressed confidence in Singh's release after 26 years, others remain divided over whether he has changed.
items.title: Odisha Christians Fear Dara Singh Release Amid Rising Church Attacks

items.summary: The Federal reports that Maldivian President Mohammed Muizzu's state visit to Pakistan, his first as head of state in over a decade, included two defence memoranda of understanding—one broad and one on maritime security—that the outlet frames as threats to New Delhi. During his three-day trip, Islamabad and Male signed 20 MoUs and set a bilateral trade target of $200 million from an existing $13 million. The article argues Malé's 'Maldives First' policy risks deepening a China-Pakistan nexus in the Indian Ocean archipelago and revives concerns over extremism. It concludes that India must sustain its engagement, though it notes New Delhi-Male ties have remained relatively stable.
items.title: Maldives' Pakistan defence MoUs alarm India over strategic shift

items.summary: The article examines John Healey’s budget, in which nearly every consumer-facing measure returned to the cost of energy as inflation rose and GDP growth was cut from 1.6% to 1%. The £100 payment to 20m households in A-D council tax bands is described as its sole surprise, funded partly by a bank surcharge lasting 15 months. EDF predicts the regulator’s price cap will rise by £466 in January, pushing an average household bill to £2,189, up from £1,568 when Labour took office in July 2024. Healey signals “deep reform of our energy system,” but the author argues the plan is still blurry and lacks urgency, with electrification policies underpowered and market reforms unfinished.
items.title: Labour’s energy policy remains half-formed amid rising bills

items.summary: Vitalii Kim, Ukraine's Minister for Veterans Affairs, told FRANCE 24 that Ukraine will fight regardless of European support. Speaking in Paris amid uncertainty over a €90 billion aid package and speculation about Trump-mediated talks, he said "we also will fight because it's our motherland." He acknowledged public exhaustion from relentless bombardment and strikes on energy infrastructure, while outlining plans to reintegrate an estimated 1.5 million veterans with expanded mental healthcare.
items.title: Ukraine's Minister Vows to Fight Despite EU Aid Uncertainty

items.summary: An 18-year-old student preparing for competitive exams died by hanging herself at a hostel in Bhanwarkuan, Indore on Tuesday night. The room stayed locked until police found her dead; no suicide note was recovered. Her roommate had left for work, leaving her alone. Police will seize her mobile phone to investigate the circumstances.
items.title: Indore Aspirant Dies By Suicide At Hostel As Police Investigate

items.summary: Brazil's main stock index fell further on Wednesday as fears over the country's fiscal outlook grew after Flávio Bolsonaro lost a surprise election and fled to the US. Finance minister Paulo Guedes said the selloff reflected unwinding of pre-election bets rather than fundamentals, with some analysts calling it an opportunity. A Bloomberg columnist linked the volatility to prediction markets that briefly generated around $130 billion in stock market wealth before it vanished.
items.title: Investors Watch Brazilian Stocks After Election-Driven Selloff

items.summary: A security guard from Mhow died after slipping and falling beneath a train while alighting at platform number two of Indore railway station on Tuesday night. Mohammad Israel, who worked for a private company in Indore, had travelled to the city for his night-shift duty. Survived by a son studying and a daughter whose marriage was fixed in Pune for two months away, he died just before the wedding preparations.
items.title: Mhow Security Guard Dies After Slipping From Train Before Daughter's Wedding

items.summary: European refineries closed a decade ago while Gulf states built new capacity, but recent Middle East conflict has damaged key facilities in Saudi Arabia and Russia. IEA chief Fatih Birol warns crude and gas prices stay elevated next year as refined-product supply cannot be rerouted like raw oil. Ukraine's drone strikes hit 30 Russian refineries—80% of national capacity, down from 6.1 million to an estimated 1.6 million barrels daily. A Trump–Putin deal sends only 300,000 tons (75,000 barrels a day) of diesel abroad, which analysts call negligible against global demand. Russia raised refining output ~25% in October to about 5 million barrels daily via local repairs, yet the shortage persists and further attacks loom after planned U.S. midterm hostilities with Iran on November 3.
items.title: Refinery Damage Deepens Global Fuel Shortage

items.summary: Asian shares fell on Oct 29 after AI-related earnings produced mixed reactions ahead of Amazon and Intel results. Hefty cash burn sent Alphabet's shares down 10% in after-hours trading, wiping nearly US$400 billion off its market value and pushing Nasdaq futures 1% lower. Microsoft beat forecasts with better-than-expected cash flows, lifting its shares by 3%. Samsung reported a record operating profit but saw its shares slide more than 4%, dragging the KOSPI index down 2.6%.
items.title: Asian shares fall as Alphabet earnings miss drags Wall St futures lower

items.summary: Microsoft shares rose more than 5% after reporting revenue and profit that beat expectations, driven by a 48% rise in its Azure cloud division during the September quarter. The company posted US$92.3 billion in total revenue and over US$36.6 billion in profit for the period ending late September, per a filing dated Oct 28.
items.title: Microsoft Shares Jump on Azure Cloud Growth

items.summary: Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at the Pro and Tell event in Los Angeles, calling it the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. The 14-inch model starts at Rs.3,49,900 and the 16-inch at Rs.4,09,900 in India; Apple lists these as maximum retail prices inclusive of all taxes. In the US, the 14-inch M5 Pro begins at $2,899 and the 16-inch at $3,399, a $400 premium over non-touch models. Pre-orders opened globally on October 28 with deliveries from November 9 across about 30 countries; Apple India lists availability from November 9. Macworld notes Apple made no claim of CPU or GPU performance gains over the equivalent non-touch M5 models.
items.title: Apple Launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro in India From Rs.3,49,900

items.summary: A Sydney court heard that Beau Lamarre-Condon, who pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in February 2024, told police he was not avoiding them despite vanishing for days. A colleague sent him an unread Instagram message urging him to contact the crime manager at eastern suburbs. He later called police saying he would come in tomorrow.
items.title: Police colleague messaged accused killer on Instagram after alleged murders

items.summary: Four traders told Reuters that the Reserve Bank of India probably stepped into the foreign exchange market on Thursday, describing the move as mild and intended to nudge prices rather than force a sharp currency bounce. The rupee closed at 95.2350 per dollar, little changed from its previous session's close of 95.22.
items.title: Traders say RBI likely intervened to steady rupee

items.summary: Asian shares fell on Thursday (Oct 29) after AI-related results produced mixed reactions, raising stakes for Amazon and Intel. Hefty cash burn sent Alphabet's shares down 10 per cent in after-hours trading, wiping nearly US$400 billion off its value and pushing Nasdaq futures lower, while Microsoft beat forecasts to lift its shares 3 per cent. VanEck's Jamie Hannah said ad revenue was hit by the AI boom but data center growth stayed solid.
items.title: Asian shares fall as Alphabet earnings miss drags Wall St futures lower

items.summary: Per Reuters, Amazon cut roughly 250 jobs at its Devices unit Wednesday via early-morning emails and messages. A spokesperson confirmed the layoffs without citing a number; the company says they aim to streamline work for future products while investing up to $220 billion this year in AI.
items.title: Amazon Cuts ~250 Jobs in Devices Unit Amid AI Push

items.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin called Elon Musk a “real genius” while outlining Moscow’s plan to develop Rassvet, its own satellite internet network operated by Bureau 1440. The remarks come as SpaceX restricts access to Starlink in October, reportedly disrupting Ukrainian drone attacks and air defences that depend on the service since Russia’s February 2022 invasion. Musk said SpaceX closed a loophole after Ukraine allegedly used civilian Starlink for offensive strikes; neither he nor Washington initially claimed responsibility. Rassvet has launched more than 30 satellites, with targets of over 900 by 2035, though its capacity remains far below Starlink’s thousands. Putin acknowledged the gap while stressing coordination between Moscow and Washington to prevent orbital interference.

Reported by Sayantani Biswas (Livemint).
items.title: Putin Praises Musk as Russia Builds Rival Starlink Network Amid Ukraine Restrictions

items.summary: Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at a Wednesday event, adding an OLED display with Dynamic Island and M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. In India the 14-inch model starts at ₹3,49,900 and sales begin on November 9.
items.title: Apple Launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro in India

items.summary: A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by 88 Tesla owners seeking full refunds for "Full Self-Driving" driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. The Seoul Central District Court found the FSD option did not promise fully autonomous driving without human intervention and that Tesla had already provided some package functions.
items.title: Seoul Court Rejects Tesla Owners' Refund Lawsuit Over Full Self-Driving Software

items.summary: Amazon cut about 250 jobs on Wednesday in its devices and services unit, which includes Kindle e-readers and tablet computers, after weeks of product rollouts. The company confirmed the layoffs following a Reuters inquiry. A spokesperson said text messages and emails were sent to workers early Wednesday morning, citing "a thorough review of our structure." Amazon also announced new Alexa-powered products.
items.title: Amazon Cuts Jobs in Devices Unit

items.summary: Amazon laid off 250 employees in its devices unit, which makes Kindle e-readers and Echo smart speakers, with cuts concentrated in software development roles. The layoffs followed an engineering memo urging developers to learn AI or risk being left behind, and coincided with five new Alexa-powered device launches. Amazon confirmed the reductions but did not disclose the number of affected employees; a spokesperson said they would help it operate more efficiently as it prepares to invest heavily in artificial intelligence this year.
items.title: Amazon Trims Devices Unit as AI Spending Rises

items.summary: OpenAI's Sam Altman expressed 'chronic disappointment' with MBA graduates who pursue outdated trends rather than embracing artificial intelligence opportunities, according to Fortune. Speaking at Stanford Graduate School of Business, he noted that while AI will transform many jobs over time, it also creates unprecedented chances for those willing to innovate. Other tech leaders like Mark Cuban and Alexis Ohanian share this optimism about AI-driven entrepreneurship.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Criticizes MBA Students for Chasing Outdated Trends Amid AI Shift

items.summary: A dispute over control of the Tata Group has drawn Indian opposition and ruling party leaders into a political confrontation, according to reporting. Rahul Gandhi alleged the Modi government is damaging the conglomerate, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman accused him of politicising commercial matters. Sharad Pawar backed Noel Tata in opposing the reappointment of Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman over procedural concerns. The corporate fight may reach courts.
items.title: Tata Boardroom Dispute Draws Congress and BJP Into Political Clash

items.summary: Amazon laid off roughly 250 employees in its devices and services division, which includes Kindle e-readers and tablets. A source familiar with the matter said no more than 250 jobs were affected, mainly software development roles. Amazon called it a small elimination of positions to operate more efficiently and align teams with product plans. The cuts follow earlier reductions in retail and corporate units this year.
items.title: Amazon Trims Devices Unit Staff Citing Efficiency

items.summary: NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weights speech-augmented language model designed to turn audio and text instructions into transcriptions across up to 40 languages in recordings as long as one hour. The single model combines transcription, speaker diarization for up to eight speakers, timestamps and translation, potentially replacing separate ASR, diarization and alignment tools. NVIDIA reports it scores best among open-weights models on the English Open ASR Leaderboards at a mean WER of 4.71%, though commercial APIs still lead. The model is offline only, with weaker accuracy on Mandarin far-field meetings.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe for Multilingual Speech-to-Text

items.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to introspect over unemployment, inflation and stalled private investment. He said voters delivered a no-confidence motion against the PM Modi government's policies in Varanasi and Nagpur. The remarks followed BJP gains of 13 of 28 Legislative Council seats across four states.
items.title: Congress' Jairam Ramesh Calls for Modi Government Introspection After BJP Losses

items.summary: The Indian Patent Office rejected a patent application from the Global Alliance for TB Drug Development, a US-based organisation, for BPaL, a tuberculosis therapy. The office cited lack of novelty and inventive step. Health experts said the decision could enable domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries.
items.title: India Rejects US TB Drug Patent Bid Over Novelty Concerns

items.summary: Amazon unveiled the next-generation Echo Dot as a smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender. According to Amazon, it includes an Eero-based feature adding up to 1,000 square feet of coverage. The device costs $100 and is available now in four colors. It also offers more bass than the previous model.
items.title: Amazon’s new Echo Dot adds built-in Wi-Fi extender, sells for $100

items.summary: Spain began a three-day mourning period after a high-speed rail collision killed 68 people and injured scores, its second such accident this year. The crash occurred Wednesday morning on the Madrid-to-Andalusia line when an Iryo train stopped and another struck it near Urda; officials said 107 more needed hospital treatment, including 15 in serious condition. Transport minister cited error and inexplicable circumstances amid safety concerns, while relatives seek news as identification efforts continue.
items.title: Spain Opens Three-Day Mourning After Second High-Speed Train Crash of the Year

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey has unveiled a package of support for households affected by rising energy costs, which he attributes to global economic storms and the war in the Middle East. In his maiden budget, he said he is setting "a new course to get energy costs down in line with Europe." Under the government's price cap, average dual-fuel bills are £1,700 a year and could rise to more than £2,100 from January.
items.title: John Healey Unveils Household Energy Support Package in Maiden Budget

items.summary: Japanese government bonds were steady on Thursday, the day before the Bank of Japan's monetary policy meeting, with strong demand at a 2-year auction supporting prices. The benchmark 2-year yield eased half a basis point to 1.895 per cent after an earlier rise. A bid-to-cover ratio rose to 4.03 from 3.89 last month. Analyst Yuhi Kawano of Mizuho Securities said the market saw less hawkishness than expected, which should support yen bonds.
items.title: Japanese bond yields hold steady ahead of Bank of Japan decision

items.summary: An editorial published by CGTN, with opinions attributed solely to its authors, presents China's ecological restoration as a model for biodiversity conservation ahead of the UN COP17 conference. It describes decades of forest expansion, grassland recovery and desertification control, and outlines an approach combining targeted intervention with natural recovery under the phrase 'minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery.' The article cites examples such as the Shan-Shui Initiative, recognized among the UN's first World Restoration Flagships, and a managed high-tide roost called 720 at Tiaozini in Yancheng. It concludes that China can contribute to lasting biodiversity gains through integrated restoration, scientific inquiry and international cooperation.
items.title: China Frames Ecosystem Restoration as Model for Global Biodiversity

items.summary: African and Chinese officials called for stronger cooperation against corruption, framed during the China-Africa Anti-Corruption Forum in Cairo. Amr Darwish cited estimates that Africa loses about $148 billion annually to corrupt practices—about 25% of its gross domestic product—and said research centers calculated the figure while noting no accurate statistics exist. Abdel Fattah al-Sisi stressed tackling corruption needs coordinated action, and Sabry El Gendy urged strict laws over awareness campaigns alone.
items.title: China and Africa Push Anti-Corruption Cooperation at Cairo Forum

items.summary: Sensex jumped more than 600 points above 73,860 while Nifty 50 gained 175 points to near 22,875. Broader markets rose up to 0.6%, with Adani Ports leading gains at over 4%. The rally followed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman saying long-term capital gains tax talks were ongoing and foreign investors net-bought equities worth around Rs 872 crore on Wednesday, though analysts say a trend reversal is yet to be confirmed.
items.title: Indian indices surge on tax-cut hopes and FII buying

items.summary: Motor manufacturer Nidec said it will miss its target of obtaining an unqualified opinion on its fiscal 2025 securities report by month's end. It cannot complete procedures sought by audit firm PwC Japan Group, including confirming whether executives or employees were involved in irregularities. The company plans to submit an internal control document to the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Friday; the exchange will decide within several months whether to keep Nidec listed.
items.title: Nidec Misses October Audit Opinion Deadline Amid Ongoing Scandal

items.summary: Fishers in Indonesia's Maluku Islands report that intensifying rough seas are keeping them ashore and shrinking catches as the current El Niño strengthens, according to early local monitoring and interviews. Blue Ventures' partners recorded average catch per trip falling to 3.6 kilograms (7.9 pounds) in April-July 2026 from 8.3 kg in 2025 and 10.6 kg in 2024, though the group says this does not prove fish populations are shrinking; instead, higher waves limit fishing time and range. A global study linked extreme ocean heat and low productivity to lower catches worldwide but did not cover Maluku. The World Meteorological Organization warned the El Niño could become one of the strongest since 1950.
items.title: Rough Seas and El Niño Strain Maluku Fishers

items.summary: The UK Registrar of Companies published a gazette notice on October 27, 2026 stating that Hamleys Franchising will be struck off the register and dissolved unless an objection or cause is shown within two months. The unit relates to Reliance's acquisition of British toy retailer Hamleys for about Rs 620 crore.
items.title: UK Strike-off Notice Threatens Reliance's Hamleys Franchising Unit

items.summary: Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury said Wednesday that Airbus could join Britain, Japan and Italy’s Global Combat Air Program (GCAP) to build a next-generation fighter after the Franco-German scheme collapsed. He called joining “potential” among other options for governments to decide. The three countries have allotted more than $5.5 billion, aiming for service by 2035.
items.title: Airbus CEO Signals Possible GCAP Fighter Partnership

items.summary: This year marks the 90th anniversary of the completion of the Long March, a two-year strategic manoeuvre spanning thousands of miles that kept the Chinese revolution alive. Cambridge historian Hans van de Ven argues it was more than a national event: he contends the march and broader revolutionary experience shaped China's destiny while profoundly influencing twentieth-century world history.
items.title: Historian Frames Long March as Global Turning Point

items.summary: Zhang Deyong, a researcher at China's National Academy of Economic Strategy and Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, argues that preventing hidden local government debt risks is essential to balancing development and security. He says resolving such debt must accompany economic growth through 4.4 trillion yuan ($660 billion) in new special-purpose bonds this year, which support major projects while replacing existing hidden debt.
items.title: China Strengthens Oversight of Local Government Debt

items.summary: Sanrio, maker of Hello Kitty, apologized and ended its merchandise partnership with the Japanese spy drama Vivant after backlash in China. Chinese state media and social users condemned the show for depicting torture tactics against a Japanese operative. Sanrio said it terminated the collaboration because the content contradicted its values of care and harmony.
items.title: Sanrio Ends Hello Kitty Partnership With Controversial Japanese Spy Drama After China Backlash

items.summary: CarTrade Tech’s Q2 revenue from operations reached Rs 213 crore, up 10% to Rs 76 crore EBITDA. Global brokerage Nomura raised its target price for the stock to Rs 3,377 from Rs 3,340, implying a 37% upside. The brokerage noted an adverse base effect in the quarter but expects margin expansion and continued growth potential at OLX India.
items.title: CarTrade Tech shares fall as Nomura raises target price
