items.summary: Analysts say largecap stocks are stabilising first while the broader Indian market continues sliding, a divergence they warn may not signal a full recovery. Vikas Gupta of OmniScience Capital told ET Markets that mid- and smallcaps had traded at premium valuations even with higher growth expectations, whereas largecaps were already reasonably valued; as rate-hike odds rose, investors stopped paying those premiums. Kotak projects Nifty earnings to grow 18% in FY2027 and 13% in FY2028, noting the benchmark trades at about 18.3 times FY2027 estimates. Gupta cautioned that largecap strength is an early leadership shift rather than a confirmed bottom, with crude prices and macro uncertainty still weighing on markets; he also warned against broad conclusions from index-level earnings given concentration in few stocks.
items.title: Largecaps hold up as Indian market slides on valuation reset

items.summary: Custodial doctors and senior lawyer John Lawrence SC say adult and youth prisoners in the Top End of the Northern Territory are struggling to access health care and medication as prisoner numbers rise. Doctors speaking at a Centre for Disease Control conference said staffing pressures limit patient contact, while Mr Lawrence called conditions “gross overcrowding” and described the territory’s imprisonment level as second highest in the world. A corrections spokesperson said decisions on medical treatment rest with NT Health and that escort requirements vary by circumstance; it disputed claims that external appointments automatically cause lockdowns. NT Health did not respond to a request for comment.
items.title: NT custodial doctors report barriers to prisoner healthcare amid overcrowding

items.summary: An analysis of Australian Early Development Census data says Canberra children increasingly start school with complex needs and developmental vulnerability rising in every cycle since 2015. The report places the territory second-lowest nationally for on-track development, with one child in four showing significant concern. Experts note mounting family pressures, thinning carer-child bonds, less reading at home (75% in 2015 to 69% in 2024), and high screen use among children and parents.
items.title: Canberra Children Face Rising Developmental Vulnerability, Report Finds

items.summary: The Supreme Court permitted West Bengal's use of the 'logical discrepancy' category during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls, calling it an interim arrangement while reserving judgment on its legality. The court said Bihar's May 27 judgement was not binding precedent. Notices reached about one-third of Delhi's draft roll; more than 94% were cleared for inclusion ahead of publication on December 4.
items.title: Supreme Court permits logical discrepancy category in Bengal SIR as interim measure

items.summary: DartSolar LLC, a clean technology firm in Los Angeles, California, has finalized production plans for an expandable vehicle-integrated solar array that mounts onto standard roof racks and truck beds without structural changes. The system uses modular units that contract to about 15 square feet and deploy up to 457.2 cm long, with configurations producing between 1000 W and over 2000 W of capacity. Housed under a protective shell and tested at speeds up to 160 km/h, the array is intended for off-grid power rather than EV charging; DartSolar estimates it adds approximately 16 to 32 km of driving range daily under typical exposure.
items.title: DartSolar Unveils Expandable Vehicle Solar Array With Up To 2 kW Output

items.summary: Ballard Power Systems, through its GeoPura subsidiary, introduced the HPU Agile-H, an 80 kW towable hydrogen generator designed to replace diesel generators on space- or noise-constrained job sites. Built by Siemens Energy and powered by a Ballard PEM fuel cell with integrated battery storage, it delivers continuous power at 50/60Hz using green hydrogen. Units can run off-grid, synchronize with the grid, or operate standalone, and multiple units may connect in parallel for higher loads.
items.title: Ballard's GeoPura Launches Towable Hydrogen Generator for Off-Grid Power

items.summary: Airbus chief Guillaume Faury said Wednesday the European plane maker could join a British-Japanese-Italian consortium to build a next-generation fighter after a Franco-German rival collapsed over design disputes. Airbus had represented Germany and Spain in that scheme, which failed in June with Dassault Aviation unable to agree on a design with Airbus and the German military. Faury called joining Britain's Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) only a 'potential' solution among others, noting governments must decide timing. The three countries have allocated more than $5.5 billion (€4.7bn), targeting service by 2035; Dassault now builds alone to replace the Rafale.
items.title: Airbus Seeks UK-Japan-Italy Fighter Partnership After Franco-German Deal Fails

items.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, defeated right-wing candidate and son of jailed Jair Bolsonaro, said Wednesday he is the country's rightful leader after fleeing to Florida for self-imposed exile. In a statement on his X account he called himself "the elected president" before revising it to "leader." His arrival signaled continued upheaval in Brazil, where leftist President Lula won the 2022 runoff.
items.title: Bolsonaro Calls Himself Brazil's Leader After Fleeing to US

items.summary: Spain's deadliest rail accident in 2026 killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100 when a Renfe train struck a stationary Iryo service near Urda, province of Toledo. The collision occurred on Wednesday morning as both trains headed toward Seville. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said an automatic security system malfunctioned around 8.30 am, halting trains along the affected stretch covering about 63 to 69 kilometres. He described it as inexplicable that a Renfe train was authorised to continue while a stop signal remained active and the safety system had not been restored; Puente said it may have travelled at speeds of up to 200 kilometres per hour before colliding around 8.53 am. Drivers were cleared, but investigators are examining how the malfunction and restart decision combined. The crash comes months after a January collision killed 46 people in southern Spain.
items.title: Spanish Transport Minister Blames System Failure and Restart Decision for Deadly Train Collision

items.summary: A sessions court in Gandhinagar sentenced three Muslim men, Wasim Kureshi, Mohammad Rafiq Kureshi and Asfak Bahelim, to life imprisonment for cow slaughter. The Deccan Herald reported the judgement cited the Vedas and Manusmriti. Each man received rigorous life imprisonment and a Rs 3 lakh fine. Police reportedly seized about 277 kg of beef.
items.title: Gujarat Court Sentences Three Muslim Men To Life For Cow Slaughter

items.summary: The South Korean army reported that North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, according to local media. The launches originated from the Wonsan area while flight analysis continued. Earlier, Tokyo said Pyongyang fired what may be a ballistic missile, per the Japanese Defense Ministry. Japan's Coast Guard urged ships to avoid fallen objects.
items.title: South Korea Reports North Korean Missile Launch Toward East Sea

items.summary: A special counsel team led by Cho Eun-suk sought the death penalty for former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol at the Seoul High Court during his appeal of a February life imprisonment sentence over his December 2024 martial law attempt. Prosecutors first requested it in January, per local media and Yonhap News Agency.
items.title: South Korean Special Counsel Seeks Death Penalty for Ex-President Yoon in Appeal Trial

items.summary: A 23-year-old man from Palamu district, Jharkhand, has been detained for four months after reportedly leaving his Dubai job without informing the employer and paying an agent to return home. His father, Lalan Paswan, filed a police application urging intervention; wife Sumitra also appealed for legal help.
items.title: Indian Man Jailed in UAE After Leaving Job Without Notice, Family Seeks Government Help

items.summary: A Michigan appeals court upheld a nearly $9.7 million judgment against Henry Ford Macomb Hospital in the wrongful-death case of Cathleen Allen, who died after an infection following a tummy tuck in 2017. The jury found surgeon Vijay K. Dixit professionally negligent and held the hospital administratively negligent for failing to enforce its patient-safety procedures. Expert testimony suggested earlier intervention could have saved her life. In its October 23, 2026 ruling, the court rejected the hospital’s challenges and affirmed that policy failures contributed to a delay in treatment. The judgment included $4,336,988 for Allen’s future lost earning capacity plus other damages.
items.title: Michigan Court Upholds $9.7 Million Verdict Against Henry Ford Macomb Hospital

items.summary: Abhijit Wanjarri of Congress defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency seat in the Maharashtra Legislative Council. Counting ran over 40 hours before the result was declared. The win gives Congress its first victory in this round of council elections across four states and marks a shift from what Wanjarri calls a BJP stronghold, though he credited grassroots outreach and backing from 48 organisations.
items.title: Congress Holds Nagpur Graduates Seat in Maharashtra Council Election

items.summary: An Indian Meteorological Department study analysing rainfall and temperature from 1961 to 2020 found north India is shifting toward hotter, drier climate zones while peninsular India grows wetter. Lead author Ananya Karmakar said the North West and North East regions moved from temperate to arid steppe and from hot tropical savannah to temperate hot summer, with nearly 7% of area transformed in each; about 15% shifted toward a wetter zone in peninsular India. The authors attribute the changes mainly to rising temperatures and changing rainfall, linking them to the negative phase of the Victoria Mode. Karmakar warned the shrinking savannah and temperate zones threaten food security, water resources and livelihoods, urging their inclusion in agricultural planning.
items.title: IMD Study Maps India's Shifting Climate Zones

items.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Patna director Amit Patra said the institute has taken cognisance of anti-quota remarks purportedly made in a social media post attributed to registrar and dean (administration) Awalendra Kumar Thakur, escalating the matter to higher authorities amid an uproar. Thakur denied making the post, dismissing it as a smear campaign using synthetic media and doctored screenshots, and said he would register an FIR.
items.title: IIT Patna Investigates Alleged Anti-Quota Remarks by Registrar Amid Campus Uproar

items.summary: With nearly all votes counted after Israel's Oct. 27, 2026 election, the outcome remains unclear as coalition building begins. Turnout reached a high of more than two decades at 77.7%. The ruling Netanyahu bloc fell from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-seat parliament and cannot form the next government, marking a repudiation of his administration. Arab-majority parties gained nine seats for a projected total of 19, while opposition Yashar won about 21 seats versus Likud's expected 26. Political analyst Dov Waxman says no party holds a majority, so weeks or longer may pass before a government forms; the most likely result is another election with Netanyahu as caretaker prime minister.
items.title: Israel's Divided Vote Leaves Coalition Building Uncertain

items.summary: Police said on Thursday that the Special Investigation Team probing alleged sexual exploitation of a minor at a spa in Kovalam has arrested Vani, a woman agent from Bengaluru. She is described as the seventh person arrested and allegedly trafficked girls and women to spas after being sold by a relative of the girl.
items.title: SIT Arrests Woman Agent in Kovalam Spa Minor Abuse Case

items.summary: Greenville police say South Carolina has ruled actress Hayden Panettiere's death accidental, ending a local probe into her August overdose of fentanyl, Xanax and other drugs at age 36. Citing the medical examiner's report that found no signs of trauma, police stated in a release that "Hayden Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental." The DEA reportedly joined the investigation; it is unclear whether that inquiry also concluded.
items.title: South Carolina Rules Hayden Panettiere Death Accidental

items.summary: Israel's Tuesday night election results produced an inconclusive outcome, with neither opposing bloc securing a parliamentary majority and leaving the country without a clear route to a new government. Record turnout among Jewish and Arab voters drew many overseas supporters, though President Isaac Herzog called it a
items.title: Israel's election leaves no clear path to a government

items.summary: In the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council election, BJP won six of the 11 seats while Samajwadi Party secured three, officials said on Wednesday. The contest was seen as a symbolic battle ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. SP candidate Rajiv Yadav alleged vote manipulation and demanded a forensic recount after claiming around 1,000 votes were stolen. Separately, SP president Akhilesh Yadav accused BJP supporters of assaulting his Agra-Aligarh candidate Akash Agrawal, calling the treatment inhumane. The administration maintained that counting followed prescribed rules.
items.title: BJP Wins Six UP MLC Seats as SP Takes Three Ahead of 2027 Polls

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police issued a traffic advisory ahead of singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert at the Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium on Friday, October 30. The event is part of the Aura India Tour 2026 and is expected to draw a massive crowd. From 1 pm to midnight, restrictions will apply around over 11 roads and stretches near the venue, along with eight diversion points.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Issue Advisory for Diljit Dosanjh Concert at JLN Stadium

items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues John Healey's first budget as chancellor was ambitious in approach but lacked the resources to deliver lasting relief. While supporters praised measures offering 'breathing space' amid rising prices, critics noted each announcement was modest in value. The Office for Budget Responsibility warns household savings will fall from roughly £50bn in 2026 to borrowing by 2031, with mortgage repayments reaching 4. 25% of disposable income - the highest since 2009. The bank tax raises just £1. 5bn over 15 months against a projected £11bn from an alternative levy.
items.title: Guardian editorial weighs Labour budget's ambition against its funding shortfall

items.summary: In western North Carolina, farmer Jamie Ager is challenging Republican Jennifer Balkcom for the U.S. House seat covering the region hardest hit by Hurricane Helene. Jasmine Beach-Ferrara of the Campaign for Southern Equality said voters there were too shell-shocked to vote meaningfully in the last election but expect change this year. When incumbent Chuck Edwards dropped out after an ethics finding, Ager quickly overtook Balkcom in fundraising and turned a Republican-leaning race into a toss-up. The article portrays Ager as vague on specifics: he describes sitting with DHS 'with a six-pack' until money arrives rather than outlining policy. Meanwhile Balkcom did not respond to interview requests and repeatedly answered 'I don't know.' Residents at the Big Ivy food bank say SNAP cuts left them without aid, underscoring what voters want from their next representative.
items.title: Jamie Ager Runs as a 'Mountain Democrat' in North Carolina's 11th District Race

items.summary: Vitalii Kim, Ukraine's Minister for Veterans Affairs, welcomed by François Picard, reaffirmed that Ukraine will continue fighting Russian aggression regardless of European financial assistance negotiations. He stated: "If Europe will not support us, we also will fight because it's our motherland." The article notes this resolve masks deeper psychological and institutional challenges the country faces.
items.title: Ukraine's Kim Vows to Fight Despite EU Aid Uncertainty

items.summary: Oddsmakers now favor Benjamin Netanyahu to remain Israel's prime minister in the next government, which could take weeks or months to form amid regional uncertainty. Neither his nor his main challenger's bloc can form a majority, though he retains broad powers even in a caretaker role. Chatham House's Middle East director told Semafor that a defeat would welcome Gulf engagement while his victory would keep Saudi normalization out of reach.
items.title: Prediction Markets Favor Netanyahu as Next Israeli PM

items.summary: The Federal Reserve voted today to keep interest rates unchanged, with officials seeking more data before deciding whether further hikes are needed to curb inflation. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Gov. Lisa Cook dissented, each urging a quarter-point increase. Chair Kevin Warsh maintained his hawkish stance, warning against tolerating an inflation target above 2%, while noting the central bank will take one less vote annually starting in 2027.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady as Two Officials Dissent on Inflation Path

items.summary: Dolores Huerta, an icon of the Mexican-American community and defender of migrant workers' rights in the United States, died on Wednesday aged 96. Her family announced her death via social media and requested privacy. The labor leader co-founded the largest U.S. farmworkers' union with César Chávez, whom she accused of raping her twice.
items.title: Dolores Huerta, farmworkers' rights icon, dies at 96

items.summary: Adani group stocks rose up to 3%, adding Rs 23,000 crore to the total market capitalisation of Adani Enterprises. The flagship company's share price climbed to Rs 2,550 after it reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1,492 crore for the second quarter of FY27, down from Rs 3,304 crore in the same period last year. Jefferies forecasts 70% upside and expects its newer businesses in green hydrogen, airports, data centres, roads and copper to emerge as industry leaders.
items.title: Adani Enterprises shares jump on profit and brokerage targets

items.summary: Ternus, Apple's new chief executive and longtime hardware executive, appeared at a Los Angeles media event showcasing the company's latest products, including a folding iPhone called Duo launched in September. Analysts debate whether Apple should add touchscreens to its older product line, with Steve Jobs' past resistance cited as relevant context.
items.title: Apple Unveils Folding iPhone Duo Amid Touchscreen Debate

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk as a genius for deploying more than 5,000 satellites into orbit. Speaking at an exhibition in Moscow during the Russia-Africa summit, Putin said Russia is developing its own satellite internet network and remains in contact with American partners despite political tensions.
items.title: Putin Calls Musk a Genius as Russia Builds Starlink Rival

items.summary: Shares were mixed ahead of European markets opening after Google parent Alphabet’s earnings came in lower than expected, weighing on big technology stocks amid high investor expectations tied to the artificial intelligence boom. Shares of Alphabet fell about 10% in after-hours trading as disappointing quarterly revenues raised questions over its ability to justify large AI investments, while Microsoft gained nearly 3% on better-than-expected results.
items.title: Asian and US Markets Mixed After Alphabet Earnings Miss

items.summary: Google-parent Alphabet reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 28, with CEO Sundar Pichai noting a half-trillion-dollar annual revenue run rate and 25% growth. Shares fell nearly 10%, reportedly because the company missed profit projections and raised AI spending past $50 billion. Analysts had expected less cash burn and higher capital expenditures; net income also declined from the prior year, while cloud revenue beat estimates.
items.title: Alphabet's Q3 Misses Spark Share Drop Despite Revenue Growth

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of 'criminally destroying' the Tata Group, prompting Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to counter that he was politicising commercial and legal matters without evidence. The exchange centres on a dispute over chairman N. Chandrasekaran's proposed five-year reappointment at Tata Sons, which Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata reportedly challenged after alleging procedural irregularities at the September 17 board meeting.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Modi Government of Destroying Tata Group as Political Battle Escalates

items.summary: Apple opened pre-bookings for eight new devices across tablets, laptops, desktops and smart-home gadgets in India. Prices start at ₹18,900, with sales beginning between 30 October and 13 November depending on the model.
items.title: Apple launches eight new products in India with pre-orders open

items.summary: Microsoft reported a 19 per cent year-on-year rise in revenue to $92. 3 billion for the July–September quarter as it began fiscal year 2027, driven by cloud growth. CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood said results beat expectations across revenue, operating income of $45. 9 billion (up 21 per cent) and net income of $36. 6 billion (up 32 per cent). Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63. 9 billion, a 30 per cent increase; Azure grew 48 per cent. The Devices and Consumer segment fell 3 per cent to $15. 5 billion.
items.title: Microsoft Opens Fiscal 2027 With Cloud-Driven Revenue Jump

items.summary: According to a report by The Information, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model when training their latest models. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro last week; DeepSeek launched V4.1-Flash 1017 on October 17. This distillation practice has become contentious amid intensifying US-China technology competition, with firms arguing it lets rivals copy advanced capabilities faster and cheaper.
items.title: DeepSeek and Moonshot AI Trained Models Using OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra

items.summary: Apple unveiled an overhauled, thinner and lighter MacBook Pro featuring a touch screen, its first Mac with an OLED display and Dynamic Island. The 14-inch model is priced from $2,899; the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. A top configuration costs $14,549. Chief hardware officer Johny Srouji called it a “monumental step forward for the Mac,” while CEO John Ternus introduced it on stage.
items.title: Apple Launches Touch-Screen MacBook Pro With OLED Display

items.summary: Shell reported its second-highest profit ever at US$10.8 billion (S$13.8 billion) for the third quarter, announced Oct 29, driven by record oil refining margins of US$42 a barrel versus US$24 prior to wars curtailing fuel-making capacity; adjusted net income topped analyst estimates of US$10.2 billion as its Chemicals and Products segment reached US$3.86 billion.
items.title: Shell reports second-highest profit ever as oil refining hits record

items.summary: Singapore Airlines has signed a binding deal, dated Oct 23 and announced on Oct 28, to purchase up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation sustainable aviation fuel over three years from Aether Fuels’ Singapore plant at Pulau Bukom. Deliveries begin in 2028. The agreement builds on a memorandum signed in 2025. It uses biomethane and industrial waste gases instead of lipid-based feedstocks, marking SIA’s first purchase using this new technology as part of its net-zero carbon emissions goal by 2050.
items.title: Singapore Airlines commits to buying Aether’s sustainable aviation fuel

items.summary: A data page tracks Amazon's publicly disclosed layoffs in 2026 at roughly 17,250 positions. The day before the cuts, Amazon published a September memo urging software engineers to use AI for real customer problems rather than usage metrics. Amazon links the restructuring to management simplification and prior overhiring during the pandemic.
items.title: Amazon's 2026 Layoffs Total Around 17,250 Across Multiple Rounds

items.summary: Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in after-hours trading Wednesday, erasing tens of billions of dollars from the $4tn company. Net profit slid 25% to $26.2bn for July-to-September, well short of FactSet expectations, amid an ad slowdown and continued big AI spending. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6bn, slightly below forecasts.
items.title: Alphabet shares plunge after profit miss and heavy AI spending

items.summary: A Georgia family was devastated after learning months later that their four-year-old pug, Cha Cha, had been taken home by a veterinary clinic employee instead of being euthanised. The revelation came through a Facebook post; the dog was subsequently put down when the family sought answers from Senioa Animal Hospital in Coweta County. Owner Rebecca Belote filed a complaint with the Georgia State Board of Veterinary Medicine over the handling of her pet's case.
items.title: Georgia Family Discovers Euthanised Pug Was Alive After Facebook Post

items.summary: Samsung Electronics said on Thursday it expects an AI-driven memory chip shortage to deepen next year, following a nearly ninefold quarterly profit jump. Investors were disappointed by the lack of detail on returning its windfall and slightly weak earnings, sending shares down more than 6 per cent. Samsung echoed rival SK Hynix's upbeat outlook but gave no shareholder-return plans until January.
items.title: Samsung Forecasts Deepening Chip Shortage Amid Investor Disappointment

items.summary: On Thursday in New Delhi, the Congress party mocked supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party for flagging a deliberate misspelling of Union minister Nirmala Sitharaman's name as 'Sitarama' in Rahul Gandhi's social media post. Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate said the typo was a strategy to gain attention and thanked BJP followers for amplifying it, while Rahul defended his remarks amid an ongoing dispute over Tata Sons leadership.
items.title: Congress calls Rahul Gandhi's Sitarama misspelling typo marketing, mocks BJP

items.summary: Anti-dam protests over a pre-feasibility survey of the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project have prompted heavy security reinforcement at the Dite-Dime bridge in Arunachal Pradesh. Officials said 30 companies of CAPF were deployed across protest-hit districts, with three Assam Police Battalion companies stationed in Pasighat. At least four women were wounded on Oct 23 during a 12-hour bandh, and more than 150 supporters allegedly threw stones at security personnel.
items.title: Security fortified at Arunachal dam-protest bridge

items.summary: Readers react to the budget, sharing how its measures land with ordinary households. Louie, a 24-year-old London chef earning between £37,000 and £40,000, says hospitality wages are too volatile to save for a home; he is hopeful about the new Your First Home scheme but expects to wait until his late 20s or early 30s. Business owner Graham Robinson earned £126,000 last year yet has little left after tax and rising mortgage costs. Helen sees her mortgage jump by more than £600 a month. Pensioner Peter Pillinger welcomes scrapping gas standing charges but questions how people live on the state pension alone. Florist Danielle Walker says fuel price rises squeeze small businesses, while Jonny Roberts finds universal credit housing support out of step with real rents and frustrated that no local housing allowance uprating was announced.
items.title: Budget readers weigh in on cost of living squeeze

items.summary: Lloyds chief financial officer William Chalmers called the budget's bank tax rise a temporary measure, as the lender reported doubled quarterly pre-tax profits of £2.3bn. Shares fell 3.1% despite strong results after revenue missed expectations by 1%, per Jefferies analysts.
items.title: Lloyds CFO Calls Bank Tax Increase Temporary Amid Bumper Profits

items.summary: Pauline Hanson and One Nation accuse Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of trying to exert undue political influence by offering the new MP David Farley an unsolicited additional staffer, which they say could cost taxpayers up to $200,000 in salary. The offer came outside a prior request for more staffers, with no reason given. Farley rejected it but did not rule out joining Labor.
items.title: One Nation accuses Albanese of undue political influence over MPs

items.summary: Residents of Bengaluru are protesting tree loss from proposed flyovers and tunnel roads, with some conducting independent surveys to challenge official estimates. In Indiranagar, the project's detailed report estimated 89 trees would be felled and 235 within its construction width, but residents counted 1,001 trees along a surveyed stretch, prompting them to file a petition now before the Karnataka High Court. As a result, Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited dropped one flyover segment while awaiting the court decision. Ecologists note that compensatory planting and tree transplantation cannot fully offset losses, as saplings take decades to mature and offsets often occur away from affected areas.
items.title: Bengaluru Residents Challenge Tree Loss in Flyover Projects

items.summary: Nasdaq futures fell Thursday as mixed earnings from Alphabet and Microsoft tested the AI trade, amid focus on a pending inflation reading after the Federal Reserve held rates. Alphabet slid 10.5 per cent over weak search advertising results and faster cash burn, while Microsoft rose 3.5 per cent on strong cloud growth. Jeremy Saltzberg of Check Capital Management said investors are scrutinizing monetization timelines versus spending. Dow E-minis were up 185 points; S&P 500 E-minis down 31 points; Nasdaq 100 E-minis down 365 points, or 1.22 per cent. Intel and Amazon report after the close.
items.title: Mixed Big Tech Earnings Weigh on Nasdaq Futures

items.summary: The Liberal Democratic Party, Japan Innovation Party and Democratic Party for the People approved Thursday a plan to cut 31 Lower House proportional representation seats, ending a ruling-coalition versus opposition dispute. The three intend to pass related legislation by Dec. 12. The JIP accepted fewer cuts than it wanted while DPP agreed to more; both parties said they compromised because of coalition and Upper House constraints. Fujita told reporters the deal achieved about 70% of their pledge toward a roughly 45-seat reduction.
items.title: Three Japanese parties agree on smaller Lower House after seat-cut standoff

items.summary: On Oct 29, Jordan Football Association chief Prince Ali bin Hussein pledged full cooperation with any Asian Football Confederation judicial review after accusing FIFA President Gianni Infantino of hijacking the recent AFC Congress for political purposes. The AFC said no member requested to speak and would refer his statements to its judicial bodies. Ali clarified his earlier remarks were a statement of principle, not an allegation against any person.
items.title: Jordan FA chief pledges cooperation with AFC review

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey pledged a reduction in the welfare bill ahead of the next general election, telling BBC Radio 4's Today programme that helping young people out of work is the government's 'moral duty'. His comments follow Conservative and Reform UK claims about rising benefits costs. The Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts welfare spending reaching £353bn this year and £431bn in 2031/32.
items.title: Chancellor pledges welfare cut citing moral duty to youth

items.summary: A Tokyo court ordered local assembly member Hiromi Muramatsu Thursday to pay ¥1.1 million ($6,972) in compensation for outing award-winning author Li Kotomi on social media, ruling it an unlawful invasion of privacy. The Tokyo District Court found that Muramatsu disclosed her gender identity and sensitive personal information without consent. Judge Yohei Motomura said the material was highly personal with no reasonable justification.
items.title: Tokyo Court Orders Assembly Member to Pay ¥1.1 Million for Outing Author

items.summary: In central Mozambique’s Tónduè Forest, uncontrolled fires destroyed 70% of replanted trees, leaving surviving saplings stunted. Uilson Malango, a technician with the Mocuba District Service for Economic Activities who accompanied Mongabay into the forest, said the fires broke out just after planting and wiped out most young trees across a 10-hectare area. Post-planting monitoring remains one of the greatest obstacles to forest maintenance in Zambézia province, where sites receive an average of just one visit a year — a frequency officials consider negligible. The government transferred management of Tónduè Forest to local communities in 2025, but fires recurred shortly after replanting three years earlier burned again. District data show only 30% of trees planted in 2023 survived the fires. Experts say planting alone is insufficient without sustained monitoring and community support.
items.title: Mozambique Fires and Weak Monitoring Undermine Reforestation

items.summary: Three audio recordings from the Atocha rail crash in Madrid show that a controller ordered an AVE train to resume normal speed after it was stopped behind another Iryo train, instead of the slower pace required by safety protocols. The order preceded the collision, which killed at least 68 people and injured scores more — one of Europe's worst high-speed rail tragedies.
items.title: Audio Recordings Reveal Errors Before Spain Rail Crash That Killed at Least 68 People

items.summary: El Salvador deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti in a mission to retrieve four nationals who went missing almost two weeks ago. President Nayib Bukele communicated the robust deployment to Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime earlier this week, per El Salvador's foreign ministry statement on Wednesday. The troops would also assist security efforts against gangs.
items.title: El Salvador Deploys Troops for Missing Soldiers Rescue

items.summary: Two new marine protected areas on Pemba Island's east coast, announced by the Tanzanian government at a June 2025 U.N. Ocean Conference meeting and officially gazetted in June 2026, cover about 1,300 square kilometers (502 square miles) of biodiverse waters. They emerged from collaboration between more than 20 local communities, the Tanzanian Department of Blue Economy and Fisheries, and NGOs including Wildlife Conservation Society and Blue Alliance. Fishers Omar Hamad Salim and others helped shape co-management rules; Blue Alliance reports patrols rose above 50% and illegal activity fell around 45%. Officials note hard evidence on ecosystem recovery will take time to gather.
items.title: Pemba's community-led marine protected areas aim for the 30×30 goal

items.summary: A second high-speed train disaster this year, in which a RENFE train struck an IRYO train from behind and killed 68 people, has intensified safety concerns as Spain prepares for its first national election since 2023. Transport minister Óscar Puente blamed the collision on what he called an inexplicable order from a central command center after a security system failed across 63 kilometers (39 miles), clearing the engineers of fault. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez pledged investigations and safety improvements, while his rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo demanded answers; far-right leader Santiago Abascal condemned the government as a criminal organization. Three days of mourning were declared.
items.title: Spain mourns second deadly high-speed rail crash before election

items.summary: The nation's largest grid operator, PJM Interconnection, is starting a stakeholder process to reform market rules that would let new batteries connect more easily to existing power plants and solar or wind farms. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission directed these Surplus Interconnection Service changes in 2024, but PJM had approved only two of 14 requests as of November 2025. Jon Gordon of Advanced Energy United said the Market Implementation Committee will consider next steps at its Nov. 4 meeting, with possible completion by April 2027. Gavin Ahern noted SIS has tracked 44 gigawatts of historical project requests. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Umed Paliwal estimates PJM could add 24 GW through surplus interconnection and save developers more than $31 billion in costs.
items.title: PJM Begins Reforming Rules for On-Site Battery Additions

items.summary: The state of Michigan awarded nearly $1.9 million across five organizations in late September to investigate ways to reduce emissions from heavy-duty industrial operations, including the Detroit Zoo and Bell's Brewery. The zoo received a $260,000 grant to model campus-wide decarbonization for its 2028 centennial master plan, while Bell's Brewery will use its $350,000 award to design thermal-energy efficiency at its Comstock facility. New Belgium Brewing aims to cut direct carbon emissions by 55% by 2030 from a 2019 baseline. The awards support one of four green-energy programs under outgoing Gov. Gretchen Whitmer aimed at full carbon neutrality by 2050, and participants will join the Michigan Industrial Clean Innovation Partnership before an August 2027 deadline.
items.title: Michigan Grants Zoos and Breweries to Cut Industrial Emissions

items.summary: Ofcom has published recommendations on how social media platforms can verify that users are over 16 ahead of the UK's planned ban, due in March next year. The regulator proposed four methods beyond traditional ID: photo ID matching, banking-based checks, face age estimation technology, and digital ID services. Ofcom CEO Dame Melanie Dawes said these approaches prioritise privacy while placing implementation responsibility on tech companies. Some firms, including Meta, have instead called for device-level blocking via app stores operated by Apple and Google. The regulator noted it lacks a firm figure for how many adult accounts would need to prove their age but acknowledged the number could be large.
items.title: Ofcom Recommends Methods for Social Media Age Verification

items.summary: Gary King and Steven Worthington report that AI-generated reviews, built on Claude Opus 4.8, outperform high-quality human expert reviews across every measure they constructed. They note the result may inform journal policy with trade-offs between speed and quality, reduced adversarial interactions, improved experiences for editors, reviewers, authors and readers, and advances in science. King adds that AI errors align ideologically with authors 97% of the time, matching an earlier human estimate.
items.title: AI Outperforms Human Experts in Article Reviews

items.summary: Struggling small businesses along Sydney's Southwest Metro line are hoping the new Sydenham to Bankstown extension, which opens Friday after running a year longer than forecast, brings customers back. Owner Talia Gill of Casablanca near Marrickville station had considered closing within a month of losing almost 10 staff when foot traffic dropped sharply in 2024. Her neighbour Nora Lee said her business lost 40 per cent of its customers this year. Both women describe the reopening as their last hope, though Ms Gill acknowledged uncertainty about whether it will turn things around.
items.title: Sydney Metro Opening Offers Hope for Struggling Businesses

items.summary: A national childcare commission is set for discussion at a meeting of education ministers, following renewed calls for reform after Four Corners aired CCTV footage of a trainee worker assaulting a 13-month-old boy 55 times. Early Childhood Education Minister Jess Walsh said the commission could improve strategic planning and oversight amid an oversupply in some areas and shortages in others. The government also faces questions over supervision rules, with Ling jailed for four years after pleading guilty to 82 assaults.
items.title: Education Ministers Consider National Childcare Commission After Abuse Exposure

items.summary: The Air Force Sports Complex near Lok Kalyan Marg has reportedly been shut since Monday, after maintenance staff and contractual employees were told not to report for duty. The Tribune reported the closure; Hindustan Times said members received messages that it would stay closed from 5.00am on 28 Oct till further orders. Mint could not independently confirm the report. An official dismissed demolition speculation, saying no heavy machinery had entered and questioning JCB sightings near Jaipur Polo Ground. The Centre reportedly wants to reclaim the land for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, following a 2017 eviction notice; its purpose remains unclear.
items.title: Air Force Sports Complex Closure Amid Land Reclaim Move

items.summary: A research team from China’s Hebei Normal University of Science and Technology, with the Hebei Technology Innovation Center for Photovoltaic Module Manufacturing Equipment, developed an electromagnetic-thermal strategy to improve heating uniformity in photovoltaic module laminators. The approach combines stepped aluminum magnetic shielding, zone-specific currents, and temperature-based current control to distribute heat more evenly across a large steel plate. Full-scale prototype tests reported that measured temperatures at all 13 monitoring locations stayed within 148–152 C, with a maximum difference of approximately 3.1 C.
items.title: Hebei team improves heating uniformity in PV laminators

items.summary: Dictionary.com named “maxxing” its Word of the Year for 2026, announced on October 26. Steve Johnson, Dictionary Media Group’s director of lexicography, said usage increased more than 1,000% since last year, a figure drawn from media analysed by Dictionary.com. Another estimate compared August 2026 with the average monthly rate during 2025, showing almost 19 times that earlier level; these figures measure different comparisons and should be understood separately.
items.title: Dictionary.com Names Maxxing Its 2026 Word of the Year

items.summary: Real Madrid formally apologized to China over controversial remarks by player Kylian Mbappe, sending a letter to China Media Group (CMG) through La Liga on Wednesday. The club expressed respect for China and its fans and included Mbappe's own apology reaffirming his respect. CMG had earlier rebuked the remarks as crossing a red line beyond free expression, saying they hurt Chinese people and that the club bore responsibility.
items.title: Real Madrid Apologizes to Chinese People Over Mbappe's Remarks

items.summary: Liu Yandong, former Chinese vice premier and state councilor, died of illness on Wednesday in Beijing. A file photo attributed to Xinhua shows her before the announcement. She was 81 years old. Official statements described her as a loyal communist fighter and an outstanding leader in united front work and education, science, technology, health, women's and children's affairs.
items.title: Former Chinese Vice Premier Liu Yandong Dies at 81

items.summary: Spain entered three days of mourning on Thursday after a high-speed train collision killed 68 people and injured scores. The crash, Spain's second such disaster this year, occurred Wednesday morning when a Renfe service struck a stationary Iryo train in Castilla-La Mancha. Transport Minister Oscar Puente cited an automatic control system failure and described the decision to resume traffic as inexplicable.
items.title: Spain Begins Three Days of Mourning After Deadly Train Crash

items.summary: City Union Bank reported a 27% year-on-year rise in second-quarter net profit, reaching Rs 416 crore. Net interest income jumped 31% to Rs 873 crore and gross profit rose 40% to Rs 661 crore for the quarter ended September 2026. The bank posted a half-yearly profit after tax of Rs 798 crore, up 26%. Share prices climbed roughly 7%, with analysts Jefferies and Nomura raising target prices on improved profitability and capital adequacy above regulatory norms.
items.title: City Union Bank Shares Rise on Strong Q2 Profit

items.summary: Renault Group and French energy company EDF signed an agreement in summer 2027 to launch a home vehicle-to-grid charging service in France, combining electric vehicles, bidirectional stations and smart management. The offer targets private customers of Renault’s Renault, Alpine and Dacia brands. Eligible cars can feed battery power back into the grid while charging. EDF installs chargers via its IZI by EDF service; Dreev, an EDF–Nuvve joint venture, supplies the platform.
items.title: Renault and EDF plan scaled V2G home charging for 2027

items.summary: At the India Today Health Wealth Summit, Union Health Minister JP Nadda criticised Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge over a remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said he felt ashamed of the language used and condemned the party for justifying it as reflecting mental bankruptcy. The row followed heated remarks Kharge made at an event in Patna.
items.title: Nadda Criticises Kharge Over Modi Remark

items.summary: Leaders from 21 opposition parties met at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to plan a public impeachment proceeding against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with Meira Kumar slated to preside. The event follows the refusal by electoral authorities to accept their formal notice and precedes an opposition rally on November 1st.
items.title: Opposition Plans Impeachment of Election Commissioner Amid South State News

items.summary: Vinit Kumar Dubey's family alleges he was detained and tortured in Russia to force him into the war in Ukraine. His 17-year-old sister said she had not heard from him since October 7, after he travelled to Russia on October 1 following a Telegram job offer for around $1,200 monthly at a food storage facility. She alleges his work was changed to delivery and that someone called the family claiming he faced a narcotics case. Bilaspur police SSP Rajnesh Singh said authorities were awaiting an embassy response; collector Sanjay Agrawal said the district administration had also approached the MEA. The Indian embassy and MEA have not issued statements so far, per PTI reporting by Hindustan Times.
items.title: Indian Family Alleges Brother Tortured in Russia Over Ukraine War Role

items.summary: The BJP mocked Congress over its result in the recent MLC elections, held across 28 seats in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka on October 23. Union Home Minister Amit Shah posted that Congress won '0' of the 28 seats, adding 'Ballot Box, resign.' Other BJP leaders joined with memes: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta joked Aryabhatta invented zero to count Congress's wins; Piyush Goyal captioned Rahul Gandhi at a fuel pump showing 'Zero Check Karlo Bhai!'; and Ashish Usha Agarwal declared the party's tally ZERO. The jabs followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi taunting Congress for its show despite paper ballots, which opposition parties had demanded instead of EVMs.
items.title: BJP mocks Congress with zero memes after MLC poll tally

items.summary: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is nearing Rs 500 crore in India, per Sacnilk data compiled from public sources. It opened at Rs 59.70 crore and grossed Rs 334.35 crore in Week 1, slowing to Rs 1.49 crore on Day 15 as it approaches the Rs 1,000 crore worldwide goal.
items.title: 'Jailer 2' BO Day 15: Rajinikanth and Nelson’s film nears Rs 500 crore India gross

items.summary: A boom in India's branded residences is entering its second phase, with Signature Global and Tonino Lamborghini reporting the complete sell-out of Phase 1 of their Gurugram project. The market now holds 61 schemes nationwide (24 completed, 37 in the pipeline), per a report by Global Branded Residences, ranking India third in Asia-Pacific. Yet analysts caution that premiums of 25–44% over comparable projects may not hold if execution and pricing discipline falter. Whether this momentum converts into enduring demand will depend on delivery quality rather than launch numbers alone.
items.title: India's Branded Residences Boom Faces a Staying-Power Test

items.summary: Scatec has started construction of the first phase of a 569 MW solar power plant and 100 MWh battery energy storage system in Egypt, following financing agreements totalling $217 million. The Dandara project will supply renewable electricity to Egypt Aluminium under a 25-year agreement backed by a sovereign guarantee, with commercial operation targeted for the first half of 2028.
items.title: Scatec Breaks Ground on Egypt Aluminium Solar Project

items.summary: A drought affecting the Panama Canal is tightening conditions for global shipping, according to BizDataDive. With fewer daily transit slots available, vessels are facing longer waits, higher costs, and possible rerouting. These disruptions could ripple through worldwide supply chains, impacting sectors from energy to consumer goods.
items.title: Panama Canal Drought Pressures Global Shipping and Trade Routes

items.summary: A BizDataDive piece marks the 76th anniversary since China and Finland established diplomatic ties, noting that over this period their relationship has developed into vibrant trade and investment linkages. The article frames the two nations as important economic partners through promotional posters rather than presenting new data or analysis.
items.title: China-Finland Marks 76 Years of Diplomatic Ties With Trade Focus

items.summary: Delhi Police detained two National Students’ Union of India members from outside Jamia Millia Islamia as campus protests over time-bound student union elections continued. The university has not held such elections since 2006, and students have protested since October 12, with five on hunger strike. On Wednesday the administration extended online classes until November 24 and moved end-semester examinations online, citing an unconducive campus situation. Students denied vandalism allegations and said police had detained more than 70 students since October 12.
items.title: Jamia Detains Two NSUI Members; Exams Move Online Amid Campus Protests

items.summary: According to an exchange filing, Jupiter Wagons received a Rs 1,140 crore order from the Railway Board for its participation in Indian Railways’ wagon procurement programme. The company said its private-sector order book stays strong and expects around Rs 2,000 crore of incremental inflows in Q4 FY27. Vivek Lohia, Managing Director, called it a sign of continued confidence. Shares rose about 8% but have fallen roughly 25% over three months; the market capitalisation stands at Rs 7,846 crore and the stock trades below most moving averages.
items.title: Jupiter Wagons Shares Jump on Railway Board Order

items.summary: Former Neighbours actors and crew have raised concerns about plans to use AI to help re-edit old footage into short vertical videos for mobile viewers. Fremantle, the show's producer, has partnered with US-based RoseBerry Media on the project, which will scan decades of episodes using original broadcast material rather than generating new scenes or synthetic voices. Some cast members say they did not consent to their images and voices being re-purposed, while a Fremantle spokesman says every editing stage is reviewed by humans. The companies describe it as bringing renewed value to the show's catalogue; unions are in talks about residuals for workers.
items.title: Neighbours cast and crew raise consent concerns over AI re-edits

items.summary: British King Charles’ nine-day Caribbean visit is being overshadowed by growing demands for reparations over the slave trade, though he acknowledged slavery’s injustices and said Commonwealth leaders will discuss it at their summit next week without offering an apology. Demonstrators in Nassau held banners reading “Pay us what you owe us,” while Jevon Thompson of the Ethiopia Africa Black International Congress urged full compensation. The movement is gaining momentum across CARICOM, which last month called for reparations to be added to the Commonwealth agenda.
items.title: Caribbean Protesters Demand Reparations as British King Visits

items.summary: A morning news roundup dated Oct. 29, 2026 covers several stories. In Israel, more than 500,000 outstanding ballots could reshape the parliamentary seat distribution as counting continued Thursday; projections attributed to Channel 12 put Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats versus 48 for opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot and a record combined 19 for Arab parties. A majority requires 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats, so neither side was projected to reach it. Elsewhere, Trump said Washington is communicating with Iran through mediators; Spain began three days of mourning after two high-speed trains collided in Toledo, killing at least 68 people; North Korea launched around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan toward the East Sea on Thursday; and Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself Brazil's leader while defying a court order to surrender his passports.
items.title: Israel Vote Counting Continues Amid Regional and Global News

items.summary: Customers at PNB's Sector Pi-1 branch in Greater Noida allege unauthorised withdrawals and premature closure of fixed deposits, with the disputed amount reportedly estimated at nearly Rs 35 crore. Police registered an FIR after a complaint by Shrichand of Birondi; eighteen customers filed written complaints. The bank suspended five employees including the branch manager and launched an inquiry through its anti-corruption team. The bank and police have not confirmed the total, and RBI audit delays reportedly blocked access to records.
items.title: PNB Greater Noida Branch Faces Rs 35 Crore Fraud Allegations

items.summary: North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul's defence ministry said, less than a week after South Korea proposed border talks. The launches followed recent Pyongyang weapons tests and come amid tensions over landmines that wounded three South Korean soldiers near the fortified DMZ. Analyst Lim Eul-chul called it 'a fairly high-level show of force.' (49 words)
items.title: North Korea Fires Ballistic Missiles Amid Rising Tensions
